Prehospital antibiotics within 1 h 76% (87/115); neurovascular documentation 94% (120/128); realignment and splinting 51% (45/89); photographs 86% (115); gentamicin on induction 65% (87); saline wash documented 78% (104).

result.other_findings: Post-operative infection rate 13% (16 patients); prehospital antibiotics within 1 h associated with lower infection (p<0.001). Documentation of prehospital care and intraoperative steps was frequently missing; authors recommend referral and operation note proformas and training.

result.topic: Bone health and secondary fracture prevention after hip fracture
result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic department, University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire (major trauma centre)
result.standard: UHCW trust guidelines (in line with NICE) for secondary fragility fracture prevention: vitamin D/calcium supplementation, bone-sparing medication, DEXA scan for eligible patients, bone blood tests including PTH

cycle1.dates: Patients admitted immediately before the UK lockdown of 23 March 2020 (study period February to June 2020)
cycle1.result: Pre-lockdown baseline: orthogeriatric review 88% (44/50); vitamin D/calcium 40/49 (81.6%); bone-sparing medication 17/28 (60.7%); DEXA requested 9/22 (40.1%); PTH measured 5 (10%). Post-lockdown (n=50, before intervention): orthogeriatric review 0%; vitamin D/calcium 29/50 (58.0%, P=.02); bone-sparing medication 4/22 (18.2%, P=.004); DEXA 1/28 (3.6%, P=.003).

result.intervention: Audit results presented at the monthly T&O quality improvement meeting and the 'MRS BAD BONES' mnemonic disseminated to junior doctors, advanced nurse practitioners and medical students

cycle2.dates: After dissemination of the mnemonic (within February to June 2020)
cycle2.result: Vitamin D/calcium 42/49 (85.7%, P=.003 vs post-lockdown); bone-sparing medication 21/29 (72.4%, P<.001); DEXA requested 12/21 (60.0%, P<.001); orthogeriatric review 38% (19/50).

result.other_findings: PTH was measured in no patients after lockdown or after the intervention. The return of the orthogeriatric team during the post-intervention phase is a confounder.

result.topic: National hip fracture audit impact on care and mortality
result.setting: All NHS hospitals in England; national evaluation using Hospital Episode Statistics linked to ONS mortality data
result.standard: BOA/BGS six national hip fracture standards (including surgery within 48 hours); outcome measures were early surgery (day of or day after admission) and 30-day mortality

cycle1.result: Whole 2003-2011 cohort n=471,590. Before NHFD: early surgery fairly stable (annual RR 0.987, 1.3% relative decrease per year); 30-day mortality fell from 11.5% to 10.9% (1.8% relative reduction per year).

result.intervention: Launch of the National Hip Fracture Database in 2007: national clinical standards, continuous web-based audit feedback, helpline, website and regional meetings

cycle2.result: Early surgery rose from 54.5% to 71.3% (annual RR 1.080); 30-day mortality fell from 10.9% to 8.5% (7.6% relative reduction per year; P<0.001 for difference in trend).

result.other_findings: Hospitals submitting NHFD data rose from 11 in 2007 to all 175 by 2011. Best Practice Tariff from 2010 may have contributed to the rise in early surgery.

result.setting: Trauma centre, Government General Hospital (Indira Gandhi Government General Hospital), Puducherry; general surgery trauma ward
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 204 fatal cases: road traffic injuries caused 82% of deaths; 16% under the influence of alcohol; mean delay from injury to admission 14.9 hours (median 2.5 hours); 56% had at least one halt at another facility; head injury the commonest cause of death (66%); missed injuries at post mortem in 8%; only 21% (43/204) arrived within the golden hour.

result.other_findings: Missed injuries mostly involved the cervical spine and chest wall, and all missed cervical spine injuries were in alcohol-positive patients. None of the two-wheeler riders wore helmets.

result.topic: Surgical site infection after spinal surgery abroad
result.setting: Department of Orthopaedics (spine service), Khoula Hospital, Muscat; tertiary referral centre; patients who had spine surgery in India
result.standard: not reported (compared with Khoula Hospital's own spine surgery SSI rate of about 2.7% over the same period)

cycle1.result: SSI 12% (15/125) vs 2.7% (49/1833) for local spine surgery; 10 of 15 needed surgical debridement. Four neurological deteriorations, including 2 wrong-level surgeries.

result.other_findings: Of 80 patients seen locally before travel, 54 had been advised surgery; 42 of the 54 improved, while 14 of 19 patients not relieved had been advised against surgery. Fewer than half had complete documentation from the operating institution.

result.topic: Hip fracture early mobilisation by day after surgery
result.setting: 35-bed trauma ward, James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital), Great Yarmouth
result.standard: NHFD metric: patient mobilised (standing or hoisted) out of bed by the day after surgery; target at least the UK national average of 81%

cycle1.dates: 6 months before the intervention (2019/2020, NHFD data); Hip Sprint audit September and December 2019
cycle1.result: Mean 60% of patients mobilised by the day after surgery. Hip Sprint cohort (n=60): 1.7% mobilised by healthcare assistants before physiotherapy assessment.

result.intervention: Therapy-led ward education programme for trauma healthcare assistants (1-hour 2:1 face-to-face session plus observed sign-off), ward posters and Trust media campaign, delivered over two PDSA cycles (June-July 2020 and June-August 2022)

cycle2.result: Mean 79.2% mobilised by the day after surgery after PDSA cycle 2 (from 60% in 2019). Healthcare assistant mobilisation before physiotherapy assessment 30% (n=51 cohort).

result.other_findings: After PDSA cycle 1 the rate rose to a mean of 78% but fell back to 71.8% in 2021, attributed to staff turnover. 30-day mortality fell from 10.1% to 7% between 2019 and 2022 (causality not established).

result.topic: Ottawa ankle and foot rules compliance for X-ray requests
result.setting: Emergency department, Flinders Medical Centre (tertiary hospital), South Australia
result.standard: Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria documented on adult ankle X-ray referrals

cycle1.result: 163/262 referrals met Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria; 99 of 262 (38%) did not. Compliance by profession: physiotherapists 77.3%, nurses 65.4%, consultants 61.5%, registrars/MOs/interns 54.8%. Overall sensitivity 0.59 and specificity 0.37.

result.other_findings: Registrars/MOs/interns were 2.5 times more likely than physiotherapists to refer despite not meeting the rules (OR 2.48, p = 0.026). Duration of injury was not specified on 76.3% of referrals.

result.topic: Female representation in fifth metatarsal fracture research
result.setting: Literature audit of PubMed-indexed studies, University of Kansas
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Of 472 fifth metatarsal fractures, 373 (79%) were in males and 99 (21%) in females. Studies: 18 mixed cohort (60%), 10 male only (33.33%), 1 female only (3.33%), 1 male vs female (3.33%); mixed cohorts 605/831 (72.8%) male.

result.other_findings: Only the single female-only study accounted for menstrual status, and no study investigated female performance. No study reported outcomes by sex.

result.topic: Ottawa ankle and foot rules compliance for X-ray requests
result.setting: Emergency department, South London district general hospital
result.standard: ED clerking documentation and X-ray request clinical details should contain the relevant Ottawa Ankle or Foot Rule criteria in all cases (NICE; RCR/IR(ME)R 2017)

cycle1.result: 100 ankle and 100 foot X-ray requests. Ankle: documentation compliance 74%, X-ray request compliance 43%. Foot: documentation compliance 48%, X-ray request compliance 32%.

result.intervention: First-cycle results distributed and an Ottawa rules handout given to ED staff, plus a small-group teaching session for ED junior doctors on assessing, documenting and requesting foot and ankle X-rays (mid-April 2024)

cycle2.result: Ankle: documentation 87% (p<.05), X-ray request 57% (p<.05). Foot: documentation 78% (p<.001 in abstract; p<.0001 in results), X-ray request 54% (p<.01).

result.other_findings: Ankle fracture rate rose from 17% to 22% (p=.37) and midfoot fracture rate stayed at 15%. Foot compliance stayed lower than ankle compliance in both cycles; authors suggest an electronic X-ray request template.

result.topic: Shared decision making and patient information documentation for joint replacement
result.setting: Elective orthopaedic (preoperative) clinics, University Hospital of North Tees, district general hospital (secondary care)
result.standard: NICE NG157 and GIRFT Elective Hip and Knee Pathway: documentation of patient information leaflet provision and shared decision making domains (no numerical target stated)

cycle1.result: PIL offered documented in 7% (hip) and 9% (knee); consent form copy given 30% (hip) and 50% (knee); understanding and willingness to proceed 79% (hip) and 73% (knee); recovery expectations, spinal anaesthetic and wound care ≤9%.

result.intervention: QR code-linked digital patient information leaflet (procedure, recovery, anaesthetic options, wound care, translation links) given at the end of clinic; staff encouraged to offer it and document its provision.

cycle2.result: PIL offered documented in 24% (hip) and 36% (knee); understanding and willingness to proceed 90% (hip) and 100% (knee); recovery expectations, spinal anaesthetic and wound care up to 36%; consent form copy 28% (hip) and 50% (knee).

result.other_findings: Documentation of a consent form copy did not improve. Patient survey: 100% found the digital information clear, 86% preferred it to paper and 71% felt more engaged.

result.setting: Trauma-receiving NHS hospitals in England (TARN registry)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Registry analysis: 3,792 deaths at 30 days; deprivation not associated with major trauma mortality; for minor trauma the most and second most deprived had aORs 1.35 and 1.28 for 30-day mortality.

result.other_findings: Thirty-day mortality was 10% in patients over 85 with minor trauma, higher than major trauma in all age groups under 65.

result.topic: Hospital volume and hip fracture care quality
result.setting: 68 hospitals in the nationwide Dutch Hip Fracture Audit
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Registry association study: surgery within 48 h 92.3%, orthogeriatric co-treatment 77.3%, 30-day mortality 5.6% overall; volume not associated with mortality; orthogeriatric co-treatment rose with volume up to 367 patients per year then fell (p < 0.01).

result.other_findings: No clinically relevant relation between hospital volume and time in the emergency department, surgery within 48 h or length of stay.

result.setting: Jordan University Hospital, Amman, tertiary academic hospital; elective orthopaedic surgery records
result.standard: Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR), based on Royal College of Surgeons guidance on medical record keeping (no target stated)

cycle1.result: Mean total STAR score 94.3 ± 1.6.

result.intervention: Annual teaching of practitioners on documentation using slides based on Royal College of Surgeons of England recommendations, with periodic (annual) re-auditing.
result.other_findings: Yearly audits 2016–2021 (454 records) showed scores of 95.5, 95.9, 95.7 and 96.8 for 2017–2020; consent and anaesthetic domains plateaued. Benefits on the consent form and post-op instructions were never documented, and suture details fell to 41.5%.

result.topic: Corridor care in hip fracture patients
result.setting: Ashford and St Peter's NHS Foundation Trust; NHS hospital participating in the National Hip Fracture Database
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Cross-sectional study: 11% cared for in nondesignated areas; ≥1 h 20 min in such areas associated with ≥3 ward moves (OR 4.02, 1.61–10.06); orthogeriatric ward LOS 13.4 days for bed care vs 17.2 days for >4 h 20 min.

result.other_findings: Care in nondesignated areas peaked in winter (44.6%). Multiple ward moves (OR 2.63) and prolonged LOS (OR 3.23) were associated with higher in-hospital mortality.

result.setting: Major trauma centre (two hospital sites), University Hospitals Birmingham; distal radius fracture ORIF
result.standard: BOAST 'The Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets' (2021): documentation of seven parameters (time, skin condition, padding, site, compressive exsanguination, pressure, size)

cycle1.result: Tourniquet pressure 20.5% (7/34), time 55.9% (19/34); site, padding, exsanguination, skin condition and size all 0%.

result.intervention: Teaching session for junior doctors and theatre staff, a three-part tourniquet safety checklist in theatres, and BOAST posters in theatre preparation areas.

cycle2.result: Pressure 59.0% (37/63), site 32.0% (20), padding 14.0% (9), exsanguination 13.0% (8), skin condition 11.0% (7), size 10.0% (6), time 56.0% (35).

result.other_findings: Tourniquet time did not improve and most parameters stayed below 50%. Checklist uptake was not captured; mandatory electronic operative note fields are planned.

result.topic: Confusion and vitamin D screening in hip fracture
result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Royal Shrewsbury Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: Confusion screening (AMTS) and vitamin D testing within 24 hours of admission in hip fracture patients aged 60 and over (no target stated)

cycle1.result: 27/100 (27%) screened; 14/27 (51.85%) of screens done within 24 hours.

result.intervention: Educational sessions for clinicians, nurses and ancillary staff, posters, email reminders and screening prompts added to the admission checklist (July 2023).
result.other_findings: Abnormal vitamin D levels stayed high (56% then 55%). Many patients with normal AMTS still had abnormal confusion screens.

result.setting: Dietetic Orthopaedic Physiotherapy Screening Clinic, Mater South Brisbane, tertiary metropolitan hospital outpatient clinic
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Descriptive chart audit: 32% achieved clinically significant weight loss (>5%), 58% no change, 11% gained weight; mean 182 days in care and 5 appointments per patient.

result.other_findings: 50% of the weight loss group had a very low energy diet vs 19% of the no weight loss group (p = 0.05). Only 12% of those discharged reached goal weight.

result.topic: Female representation in Achilles repair research
result.setting: Literature review of PubMed studies on operative Achilles repair
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Female representation 1783 of 10,673 subjects (16.7%) across 169 studies; 5.0% in studies of world-class athletes.

result.other_findings: 32 male-only vs 3 female-only studies; no study collected menstrual status data.

result.setting: UK national trainee-led trauma and orthopaedic collaborative projects
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 10 trainee-led collaborative projects identified during the COVID-19 lockdown (none in 2019); 6 published, levels of evidence 3 to 4.

result.other_findings: Five audits and five cohort studies; recruitment mostly via social media and data collection mostly via REDCap.

result.topic: Inpatient falls risk assessment and prevention
result.setting: Calvary Wakefield Hospital, private acute hospital, medical and surgical wards
result.standard: Hospital Falls Minimization Program and National Safety and Quality Health Service Standard 10 (Preventing Falls and Harm from Falls); eight JBI audit criteria

cycle1.result: Baseline audit showed significant opportunity for improvement in all criteria (figures not given in abstract).

result.intervention: Corrective action plan after the baseline audit (details not given in abstract).

cycle2.dates: Six months after the implementation phase
cycle2.result: Results were maintained and consistent with the first follow-up audit (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: At the first follow-up (three months), nearly all criteria improved; formal staff education improved by 46% and patient and family education by 43%.

result.topic: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency and Trauma Centre, The Alfred Hospital, Melbourne
result.standard: Evidence-based use of nerve blocks and multimodal analgesia for older patients with neck of femur fracture (no target stated)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Educational and awareness strategies on pain management for emergency department clinical staff.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in nerve block use and multimodal analgesia and a reduction in average milligrams of morphine given (figures not given in abstract).

result.other_findings: Title also reports improved triage and assessment; abstract gives no numbers.

result.topic: One-stop wide-awake hand surgery service outcomes
result.setting: Parkside one-stop wide-awake day-case surgical centre (CQC-certified primary care facility adjoined to a GP surgery), Boston, Lincolnshire
result.standard: Service targets: one-stop care, wide-awake care, 0% referral to hospital, low DNA rate, 0% litigation, patient satisfaction >99%, 0% deferral for investigation (locally set)

cycle1.result: Last 1000 consecutive cases: one-stop and wide-awake care achieved in 1000 cases; referral to hospital 0%; DNA rate 0.2%; litigation 0%; patient satisfaction >99%; deferral for investigation 0%; all cases managed within 45 minutes (median 30 minutes); 3 superficial surgical site infections and 15 delayed wound healing cases.

result.intervention: Absorbable skin sutures (introduced early 2011) replaced by non-absorbable silk sutures after audit linked them to infection and delayed wound healing.
result.other_findings: Referral diagnosis was correct in over 90% of cases (97 revised); estimated saving to the NHS of about £750,000 per 1000 cases and a mean wait of four weeks from referral to treatment.

result.topic: Paediatric forearm fracture manipulation in the emergency department
result.setting: Poole Hospital, University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics
result.standard: BOAST and GIRFT recommendations that units have protocols for manipulation of paediatric forearm fractures under procedural analgesia in the ED, avoiding admission and general anaesthesia; local standard operating procedure

cycle1.result: Pre-implementation (n=11 suitable fractures): manipulation in ED 1 (9.1%); theatre required 4 (36.4%).

result.intervention: New standard operating procedure and paediatric fracture manipulation pathway in the ED using intranasal fentanyl and Entonox, agreed with ED, orthopaedics, radiology and theatre managers; information leaflets planned after cycle 2.

cycle2.result: Third cycle (n=52): manipulation in ED 9 (17.3%); theatre required 1 (1.9%). All nine manipulable fractures were manipulated in the ED.

result.other_findings: Second cycle (n=74): manipulation in ED 11 (14.9%), theatre required 21 (28.4%); 27% of manipulable fractures were manipulated in ED and none of these later needed theatre. All manipulations were done by the orthopaedic on-call team, none by ED; documentation and consent remained areas for improvement.

result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics department, Frimley Park Hospital (750-bed NHS hospital), Surrey
result.standard: 10 handover components derived from RCS, RCP and BMA handover guidelines, each with a set standard (some patient identifiers at 100%); aim to raise compliance to 90–100%

cycle1.result: Baseline (247 handovers over nine weeks): patient name 99%, hospital number 94%, admission reason 91%, other categories 12% to 84% (date of birth 54%, location 84%, frequency of review 70%, TTO 12%); only admission reason met its standard.

result.intervention: Two-step change: extra columns (TTO, day to be seen, DNAR) added to the Word handover table, then a new intranet handover tool with drop-down boxes, date selector and multiuser access; instruction document given at induction.

cycle2.result: Sustainability re-audit of intranet tool (201 handovers, new cohort of doctors): patient name 100%, hospital number 98%, date of birth 85%; five of 10 categories met their standard (patient name, location, consultant, admission reason, frequency of review); all except TTO were above 50%.

result.other_findings: After the amended table (257 handovers) TTO rose from 12% to 31% and location fell from 84% to 77%; after the intranet tool (207 handovers) location 90%, consultant 94%, admission reason 97%, frequency of review 100% and TTO 5%. TTO stayed poorest (18%) and was dropped from the tool.

result.topic: Secondary fracture prevention after hip fracture
result.setting: Orthopaedic wards of a large district general hospital with a level 2 trauma centre
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Hip Fracture Database: all patients with hip fracture assessed for and managed with a secondary bone-protection plan (100% gold standard); SMART aim of an additional 40% per year

cycle1.result: 13.9% (n=11) assessed for bone protection; 1.3% (n=1) prescribed a bisphosphonate and 10.1% (n=8) other bone protection; 86.1% (n=68) neither assessed nor prescribed.

result.intervention: PDSA 1 awareness poster (January 2019); PDSA 2 education session for clerking and ward doctors added to induction (March 2019); PDSA 3 MDT meeting with responsibility charting, giving assessment and prescribing to the care of the elderly team (April 2019).

cycle2.dates: April 2019 (a fortnight after the MDT meeting)
cycle2.result: 100% (n=50) of patients assessed or placed on a bone-protection plan.

result.other_findings: PDSA 1 (n=27) 44.4% (p<0.01) and PDSA 2 (n=21) 76% (p<0.001); an annual re-audit of 50 patients during the COVID-19 pandemic showed 100% was sustained. At baseline 89.9% of patients and relatives were unaware of bone protection.

result.setting: Fracture clinic, Royal Shrewsbury Hospital
result.standard: Local SMART objective: satisfaction rate of at least 80% among patients assigned to PIFU

cycle1.result: 203 of 3828 fracture clinic patients (5.3%) assigned to PIFU; 183 (90.15%) received the leaflet; 41 (20.2%) used PIFU; 163 (80.3%) rated the service 5/5 and all 203 reported satisfaction, so the 80% target was met.

result.other_findings: 20 PIFU patients (9.85%) did not receive the leaflet; of all clinic attenders 2549 (66.6%) had regular follow-up and 1076 (28.1%) were discharged.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, single centre (audit approved at University Hospitals Dorset, Poole General Hospital; authors at Dorset County Hospital)
result.standard: BOAST ankle fracture standards and NICE NG37: documentation of mechanism, skin integrity, circulation, neurological examination and repeat neurovascular examination after reduction; target 100%

cycle1.result: Mechanism of injury 86%; skin integrity 54%; circulation status 54%; detailed vascular examination 17%; neurological examination 54%; sensory detail 48%; MRC motor scale 48%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 56%; overall precise documentation of clinical findings 17%.

result.intervention: Targeted education on documentation standards at induction and trauma meetings, with case-based discussion reports; made a permanent part of departmental teaching.

cycle2.result: Mechanism of injury 100%; skin integrity 100%; circulation status 88%; detailed vascular examination 88%; neurological examination 88%; sensory detail 88%; MRC motor scale 88%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 88%; overall precise documentation 88%.

result.other_findings: Re-audit identified 22 patients, 17 included after exclusions. The shorthand 'DNVI' was the main cause of incomplete records and persisted in two patients after the intervention.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis duration in spinal surgery
result.setting: Spine Unit, Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery Department, Assiut University Hospitals (tertiary spine centre)
result.standard: North American Spine Society (NASS) 2013 guideline on perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis: preoperative dose, redosing as needed, discontinuation within 24 hours for uncomplicated non-instrumented surgery

cycle1.result: All patients received a correct preoperative first-generation cephalosporin dose, but IV antibiotics continued 1–6 days followed by oral antibiotics until suture removal (up to two weeks) in all patients, with mixed agents; SSI 1 case (1.85%).

result.intervention: New local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis protocol (first-generation cephalosporin 30–60 minutes before incision, redose after 3 hours, stop at 24 hours) agreed in discussion sessions and disseminated by pamphlet and theatre poster.

cycle2.result: All patients received preoperative first-generation cephalosporin continued for only 24 hours postoperatively and were discharged on day 2; no SSI.

result.other_findings: Difference in infection rates was not statistically significant; mean postoperative stay fell from 3.33 to 2.04 days.

result.setting: Plastic Surgery Department, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust (tertiary centre)
result.standard: BSSH hand trauma standards: open fractures/joints and bites within 24 hours, other open injuries within four days, closed fractures within seven days; project target 80% compliance

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 73% (part of national BSSH-RSTN collaborative audit).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 83% (82/99); open soft tissue 97% (32/33); bites 100% (10/10); open fractures/joints 64% (9/14); tendon injuries 76.5% (13/17); closed fractures 67% (16/24), surgical fixation 50% (7/14); median decision-to-surgery time 42.7 hours.

result.other_findings: Theatre capacity caused 52% (9/17) of delays and front-end referral problems 28% (5/17). Recommendations include more trauma list capacity, expanded 52 Pre-Op clinic and MIU, education for referring units and rolling audits.

result.setting: Hip fracture unit, James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough
result.standard: Hip fracture best practice tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Warfarinised patients on oral vitamin K protocol: mean time to theatre 53.71 hours; 79% breached BPT due to anticoagulation.

result.intervention: Nurse-led 'early trigger' protocol giving 2 mg intravenous vitamin K in the emergency department before the INR result, added to the fast-track pathway.

cycle2.result: Mean time to theatre 37.61 hours (p<0.0001); 34% breached BPT due to anticoagulation; 21 (50%) operated within 36 hours and 33 (79%) within 48 hours.

result.other_findings: No thromboembolic complications or deaths attributed to the protocol; 10 patients were delayed purely by inadequate reversal. Non-warfarinised controls (n=403) had mean time to theatre 28.36 hours.

result.setting: Orthopaedic trauma list, St Richard's Hospital, district general hospital, Chichester
result.standard: RCN, AAGBI, European Society of Anaesthesiology and ASA guidelines: fasting of two hours for clear fluids and six hours for solids

cycle1.result: All 50 patients (100%) fasted beyond six hours for solids (mean 15.8 hours, range 9–24) and 49 (98%) beyond two hours for clear fluids (mean 10.5 hours, range 2–20); only 5 (10%) had correct documented fasting instructions; 31 (62%) were 'nil by mouth from midnight'.

result.other_findings: Staff survey showed poor knowledge: only 42.9% of ward nurses knew the 6 hour/2 hour rule. Only 52% received preoperative IV fluids; a 'sip till send' policy has since been introduced.

result.setting: University Hospitals Dorset, large district general hospital (emergency department, orthopaedics and virtual fracture clinic)
result.standard: Local UHD Achilles tendon rupture pathway: VTE prophylaxis, boot with wedges, non-weight-bearing advice, ultrasound within 14 days and virtual fracture clinic referral; target 100%

cycle1.result: VTE prophylaxis 110/138 (80%); boot immobilisation 110/138 (80%); ultrasound within 14 days 59/138 (43%); non-weight-bearing advice 91/138 (66%); VFC referral 132/138 (96%).

result.intervention: Results emailed with recommendations, pathway posters displayed in ED, orthopaedic team room and fracture clinic, and a new 'Ultrasound Achilles' imaging request form.

cycle2.result: VTE prophylaxis 35/44 (80.5%, p=0.91); boot immobilisation 38/44 (86%, p=0.04); ultrasound within 14 days 26/44 (59%, p=0.03); non-weight-bearing advice 29/44 (66%, p=0.99); VFC referral 44/44 (100%, p=0.01).

result.other_findings: VTE prophylaxis and weight-bearing advice did not improve. No re-ruptures or VTE events in either cycle.

result.topic: Neomycin irrigation use in orthopaedic surgery
result.setting: not reported
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Title only; no abstract available.

result.topic: Ottawa ankle rules in radiograph requests
result.setting: Emergency department, Newham University Hospital (district general hospital, East London)
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists: 100% of ankle plain-film requests for trauma should reference the Ottawa Ankle Rules

cycle1.result: 37/100 (37%) requests referenced the OAR. 21 (21%) fractures; 13 (61.9%) of these requests documented the OAR and 8 (38.1%) did not (P = 0.011).

result.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance meetings; focused education sessions for front-line clinicians and targeted briefings for radiographers who vet X-ray requests.

cycle2.result: 51/100 (51%) requests referenced the OAR (P = 0.046). 31 (31%) fractures; 26 (83.9%) had OAR documented and 5 (16.1%) did not (P < 0.001).

result.other_findings: Compliance remained well below the 100% RCR target. Authors suggest electronic OAR prompts in request systems and induction teaching for rotating doctors.

result.setting: Debre Tabor Comprehensive Specialized Hospital; elective general, orthopaedic and gynaecological surgery
result.standard: NICE guideline on routine preoperative tests for elective surgery

cycle1.result: 350 investigations requested; 71 (20.28%) ordered without justification or against NICE recommendations (about 79.71% in line). FBC requested in 240 (97.16%); inappropriate FBC in 45 patients, ECG in 5, urinalysis in 4, hemostasis in 1, CXR in 1. Indicated PT/PTT not done in 4 and HbA1c not done in 4.

result.other_findings: No patient tested without a clear indication had an abnormal result. Authors recommend an accessible institutional guideline and regular re-audit.

result.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic department, Royal Hospital for Children, Glasgow
result.standard: UK national guidelines: displaced supracondylar fractures treated by early surgical stabilisation with bicortical wire fixation; bi-columnar fixation assessed on intra-operative AP radiograph

cycle1.dates: June 2014 to December 2016 (methods state April 2014 to December 2016)
cycle1.result: Bi-columnar fixation achieved in 41/49 (84%): 7/7 (100%) cross-wire cases and 34/42 (81%) lateral-entry-only cases. Intra-articular wire in 44/49 (90%). Loss of fixation needing revision 1/49 (2%), in a case without bi-columnar fixation (1/8, 13%).

result.other_findings: One superficial infection (2%) and no deep infection or septic arthritis. Bi-columnar fixation rates varied widely between the nine surgeons (60% to 100%); a re-audit is planned.

result.topic: Patient information leaflet delivery in fracture clinic
result.setting: Fracture clinic and trauma triage, Leicester Royal Infirmary, University Hospitals of Leicester
result.standard: Green Surgery Report (UKHACC 2023) sustainability aims; local success target of at least 50% of patients preferring QR code leaflets and at least 30% cost and carbon reduction

cycle1.result: 31 (62%) reported reading printed leaflets; 38 (76%) preferred digital/QR code information; 45 (90%) owned a smartphone. All patients aged 80 or over preferred printed leaflets.

result.intervention: QR codes created for six commonly used leaflets; consolidated QR poster in consultation rooms and triage; change communicated to staff by email and meetings.

cycle2.result: 16 (80%) familiar with QR codes and able to save the leaflet; 13 (65%) preferred QR codes, 4 (20%) paper, 3 (15%) either. Estimated annual saving over £1600 and about 252 kg CO2.

result.other_findings: Preference for digital leaflets was strongly associated with younger age; older patients needed printed copies, so a hybrid approach is advised.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (acute teaching hospital)
result.standard: Locally designed trauma meeting documentation standards (no UK guideline exists); record keeping guidance from GMC, RCS England and BMA

cycle1.result: 58/90 (64%) had some documentation. Consultant on call 43%, other consultants 29%, imaging 20%, MDT concerns 7%, diagnosis 29%, laterality 22%, clear plan 63%, weight-bearing 1%.

result.intervention: Electronic trauma meeting proforma (EPR shortcut) introduced, then revised after MDT feedback (theatre checklist added); teaching video and poster for new doctors before the one-year re-audit.

cycle2.result: 71/85 (84%) had some documentation. Consultant on call, other consultants and imaging 100%, diagnosis 97%, laterality 75%, clear plan 98%.

result.other_findings: Phase 2 (11 to 20 October 2022, n=98) reached 94% documentation; phase 3 (20 to 30 October 2022, n=108) 88%, with only 6/57 (11%) completing the new theatre checklist. Weight-bearing and MDT concerns sections were later removed.

result.setting: 62 centres in 16 countries (INTELLECT collaborative, multicentre retrospective audit)
result.country: International (16 countries, 1045 patients from the UK)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Median time to antibiotics 2 h (1–5); wound debridement within 24 h in 80.2%; median time to debridement 10 h (4–20); consultant-led debridement 80%; orthopaedic and plastic joint debridement 14%. Wound infection 16.3%, deep infection 10.3%, non-union 10.9%.

result.other_findings: Treatment in settings with national guidelines was protective against deep infection (OR 0.66) and non-union (OR 0.66); soft tissue closure beyond 72 h was linked to infection, non-union and amputation, and joint ortho-plastic care protected against secondary amputation (OR 0.41).

result.setting: 53 UK NHS hospitals including 8 major trauma centres (national trainee-led collaborative, CURFFED)
result.standard: BOAST Early Management of the Paediatric Forearm Fracture (2021)

cycle1.result: Mean overall BOAST compliance 63% (42.5% to 86.9%). Pain scores 83 (20%); regular analgesia 372 (87%); complete pre-manipulation NV assessment 214 (50%), post-manipulation 147 (35%); consent 163 (38%); analgesia and advice on discharge complete 95 (23%); consultant review within 48 h 328 (78%); clinic within 7 days 238 (59%). 423/577 (73%) manipulated first in ED.

result.other_findings: Median time to first manipulation 2 h 43 min in ED versus 18 h 47 min in theatre. Only 9 of 53 sites supplied a local protocol and 8 a patient information leaflet.

result.setting: University Hospital Southampton (major trauma centre)
result.standard: BOAST ankle fracture guidance (weight-bearing as tolerated after stable fixation) and WAX trial (weight-bearing from two weeks)

cycle1.result: First weight-bearing at 2 weeks 2/42 (4.8%), 2–6 weeks 9/42 (21.4%), over 6 weeks 31/42 (73.8%) (6–8 weeks 21/42, 50.0%; over 8 weeks 10/42, 23.8%). Median 48 days (IQR 42–56); none discharged weight-bearing as tolerated.

result.other_findings: Early safety was reassuring (unplanned contact 1/42, no re-operations or loss of reduction, delayed union 2/42). Posterior malleolus fixation was linked to longer time to weight-bearing (p=0.036); re-audit planned at 6–9 months after a default WBAT-from-two-weeks pathway.

result.setting: 43 centres in 13 countries (INTELLECT paediatric subgroup, multicentre retrospective audit)
result.country: International (13 countries, 66 patients from the UK)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Median time to antibiotics 2 h; median time to primary wound excision 11 h; combined orthopaedic and plastic surgery care from debridement in 14%; consultant-led excision 71%. Wound infection 20 (12%), deep infection 8 (5%), non-union 9 (6%).

result.other_findings: Soft tissue closure beyond 72 h was associated with soft tissue infection (OR 14.67); children aged 5 or under had more deep infection (OR 16.89). About one-third of cases needing reconstruction were Gustilo IIIB/IIIC.

result.setting: Regional orthopaedic unit, emergency trauma cases, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BOAST safe use of intraoperative tourniquets: documented skin checks, isolation, exsanguination, pressure (SBP-based) and time; ischaemic time under 120 minutes

cycle1.result: Full adherence 3 (6.0%), partial 16 (32.0%), overall compliance 38.0%; not adhered 31 (62.0%).

result.intervention: After EPR introduction: survey, department emails and theatre posters; then findings presented at audit meeting and an EPR smart phrase template with drop-downs and automatic SBP calculation introduced.

cycle2.result: Full adherence 9 (18.0%), partial 22 (44.0%), overall compliance 62.0% (p=0.0005 vs 17.0% in cycle 2). Pressure documented 76%, time 94%, skin pre 56%, post 60%, isolation 60%, exsanguination 24%; pressure within standard 24 (63.1%).

result.other_findings: An intermediate cycle after EPR roll-out (June to July 2023, n=59) fell to 17.0% compliance with 0% skin and isolation documentation. Only 44% of 50 surgeons surveyed knew the BOAST guidance; mean lower limb pressure fell from 287.06 to 265.91 mmHg (p=0.007).

result.topic: Preoperative anaemia screening before joint replacement
result.setting: Four campuses (three private, one public) of a tertiary metropolitan healthcare facility, South East Queensland; primary total hip and knee replacement
result.standard: National Blood Authority Patient Blood Management guidelines: FBC, iron studies, CRP and renal function at least 6 weeks before surgery, with treatment of anaemia

cycle1.result: FBC 96% (583), renal 94.7% (575/607), iron studies 8% (49/607), CRP 2.4% (15); all recommended tests 2.4% (15). Screening 6 weeks or more before surgery 3.95% (24/607). 85 (14.6%) anaemic; 10/85 had some preoperative treatment and 1.2% (n = 1) received guideline-concordant treatment.

result.other_findings: Anaemic patients were more likely to be transfused (OR 8.65) and stayed one day longer; 21/40 (52.5%) transfusion episodes did not follow PBM guidance. A standardised anaemia pathway was being developed.

result.topic: Mental health of shielded children during COVID-19
result.setting: Children aged 2–17 registered with GP practices contributing to the SAIL databank, Wales (data linkage study)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Not an audit: a data linkage study showing anxiety or depression diagnoses or prescriptions fell during COVID-19, with new diagnoses higher in shielded children (2.0%) than the general population (1.0%).

result.setting: University Hospitals Leuven
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Most patients followed a late weight-bearing protocol; early weight-bearing was used in younger patients with lower BMI. No differences in union, complications or length of stay; fracture-related infection 1 (4%) vs 5 (2.5%), EWB vs LWB (P=0.922).

result.other_findings: Average cost of surgical management €6,419, driven mainly by length of stay; total costs did not differ between early and late weight-bearing. All open fractures followed late weight-bearing.

result.topic: Non-hip femoral fragility fracture surgery timing and weight bearing
result.setting: Seven NHS hospitals in the Wessex Deanery (Southampton, Portsmouth, Poole, Salisbury, Basingstoke, Dorchester, Isle of Wight); multicentre retrospective audit
result.standard: BOAST 'The care of the older or frail orthopaedic trauma patient' (2019) point 14: all surgery in the frail patient should allow full weight bearing and be performed within 36 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Of 342 patients with time-to-surgery data, 86 (25%) had surgery within 36 hours; 256 had surgery after 36 hours. FWB prescribed in 41 (76%) arthroplasty vs 173 (57%) fixation patients; arthroplasty patients breached 36 hours more often (n = 46, 85%) than fixation (n = 218, 72%).

result.other_findings: Fixation (n = 303, 85%) was the main treatment; FWB was achieved by 36 (87%) arthroplasty vs 121 (70%) fixation patients prescribed it. Median length of stay was 13 days with surgery within 36 hours vs 17 days after, and NWB patients were less often discharged home (21% vs 56% FWB).

result.setting: St Richard's Hospital, Chichester; district general hospital trauma and orthopaedic department
result.standard: GMC Decision Making and Consent (2020), RCS England Consent: Supported Decision-Making (2016) and the BOA-endorsed orthoconsent.com model hip fracture consent form

cycle1.result: Infection documented in 98.4%, blood clots 95.2%, bleeding 92.1%, neurovascular injury 79.4%, dislocation 77.8%, pain 74.6%, anaesthetic complications 73%, failure 68.3%, leg length discrepancy 60.3%, bone damage/fracture 50.8%, death 49.2%, wound complications 42.9%, hip stiffness 14.3%, catheterisation 0%. Diagnosis missing in 22.2% (n=14), benefits in 12.7% (n=8), responsible consultant in 28.6% (n=18), blood transfusion in 25.4% (n=16).

result.other_findings: 52.4% of consents were taken by SHOs/core trainees without formal orthopaedic training; orthopaedic-specific risks were documented less often than generic risks (p<0.00001). Patient name and date were missing beside the signature in 57.1% (n=36); induction teaching, governance presentation and posting the model form were recommended with a planned re-audit.

result.setting: Kamsar Hospital, Boké region, Western Guinea; referral hospital neonatal and general paediatric units
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 39 of 5670 admissions (0.7%) were tetanus (22 NNT, 17 PNNT); 21 (53.8%) died within 7 days (NNT 16/22, 72.7%; PNNT 5/17, 29.4%).

result.other_findings: 36/39 (92.3%) were born to unvaccinated or suboptimally vaccinated mothers; severe disease was the only factor linked with mortality after adjustment. Cases at the hospital were not reflected in WHO national reports, suggesting under-reporting.

result.topic: Preoperative epoetin for anaemia in hip arthroplasty
result.setting: Polyclinique de la Thiérache, Wignehies; single-surgeon series of primary total hip arthroplasty
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Group A (anaesthetist-prescribed EPO, 4 weekly 40,000 IU for Hb 10–13 g/dl): EPO given to 43 (6.7%); mean total dose 115,349 IU; bleeding index 2.7 ± 1.0; 5 (0.8%) transfused up to POD7.

result.intervention: Amended EPO protocol (2013) prescribed by the surgeon: two injections of 20,000–40,000 IU at 14 and 7 days before surgery for Hb <12 g/dl in patients at high transfusion risk.

cycle2.result: Group S: EPO given to 26 (3.4%) (p = 0.006); mean total dose 75,200 IU (p < 0.001); bleeding index 2.8 ± 1.0 (p = 0.375); 0 transfused up to POD7 (p = 0.021).

result.other_findings: No patient who received EPO was transfused, and EPO-treated patients had a lower bleeding index (2.2 ± 1.0 vs 2.8 ± 1.0, p < 0.001). In 2017 the protocol was changed again to Hb <11.5 g/dl and 20,000 IU doses.

result.topic: Virtual fracture clinic referral and remote follow-up
result.setting: Great Western Hospital, Swindon; 480-bed district general hospital fracture clinic and virtual fracture clinic during COVID-19
result.standard: BOAST COVID-19 guidance points 7–10: removable casts/splints in 100%; index fracture clinic appointments 100% virtually screened; follow-up by phone/video in 100%; follow-up radiographs for union in 0% (exceptions if documented)

cycle1.result: 100% removable casts; 96% virtually assessed or approved for face-to-face (197 VFC, 18 approved, 8 no approval); 97% virtual follow-up or documented reason (6/223, 2.7% without); 0.4% inappropriate radiographs for union.

result.intervention: All patients required a consultant-level senior opinion (trauma meeting, on-call consultant or VFC) before a face-to-face appointment, from 11 May 2020; email reminder to use virtual clinics.

cycle2.result: 100% removable casts; 99% virtually assessed or consultant-approved (130 VFC, 14 approved, 1 unapproved); 100% virtual follow-up or documented reason; 0.7% inappropriate radiographs for union.

result.other_findings: A simulated virtual clinic for the 26 patients first seen face to face showed 22 appointments and 13 X-ray attendances could have been saved. The one unapproved re-audit patient was a GP referral, so GP and outside referrals are now discussed with the VFC team.

result.topic: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
result.setting: Poole Hospital (University Hospitals Dorset); district general hospital emergency department and orthopaedics
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean MRI completion from arrival 13:54:49; mean MRI request from arrival 14:12:03; arrival to action plan 27:29:00; 28% stayed less than 24 hours.

result.intervention: Findings shared with ED and radiology; reserved MRI slots for suspected CES booked directly by ED with prioritised vetting; red-flag checklist and bladder scan protocol; proposed CES pathway; posters and pathway distributed to ED and orthopaedic staff.

cycle2.result: Mean MRI completion from arrival 10:39:00; mean MRI request from arrival 06:10:00; arrival to action plan 15:38 (43.1% reduction vs cycle 1); 54.4% stayed less than 24 hours.

result.other_findings: Three cycles; the second (1 June–16 July 2021, n=50) showed MRI completion 12:24:00, MRI delay from order 5:01:32 and 36% staying under 24 hours. Mean inpatient stay rose in cycle 3 (85:08:00) due to complex discharges; 8/168 (4.7%) had CES.

result.setting: Orthopaedic Department, James Paget University Hospital, Gorleston; enhanced recovery pathway for primary TKR
result.standard: Mobilisation within 24 hours after surgery, in keeping with ERAS principles and local pathway expectations

cycle1.result: 35/53 (66.0%) mobilised within 24 hours; median length of stay 2 days.

result.intervention: MAKE1 findings presented to the multidisciplinary team; reinforcement of enhanced recovery practices, better documentation of reasons for delayed mobilisation and prompt management/escalation of pain, nausea and hypotension.

cycle2.result: 57/63 (90.5%) mobilised within 24 hours; median length of stay 2 days.

result.other_findings: Pain remained the commonest barrier and was linked to longer stay (mean 5.2 days in MAKE2). No POD 0 physiotherapy assessments were documented, and no clear difference was seen between spinal and general anaesthesia.

result.setting: Royal Gwent Hospital, Newport; 774-bed district general hospital trauma and orthopaedics
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons consent standards

cycle1.result: Procedure details documented 93%; abbreviations used in 38%; procedure-specific risks documented 31%; copy offered to patient 12%.

result.intervention: Cycle 1 (January 2018): induction and departmental teaching on consent plus senior review of consent forms on the morning ward round. Cycle 2 (August 2018): hip fracture proforma with pre-printed procedure-specific consent risk stickers and induction teaching on their use.

cycle2.result: Procedure details documented 100%; abbreviations 7%; procedure-specific risks documented 67%; copy offered to patient 8%.

result.other_findings: After teaching alone (January 2018, n=26) abbreviations fell to 20%, procedure-specific risks rose to 72% and copies offered to 48%. Sticker supplies ran out and formal use fell below 75% of forms, and offering a copy fell once it was not prompted.

result.topic: Native hip dislocation time to reduction
result.setting: Major trauma centre, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff; plus survey of Welsh EDs and UK MTCs
result.standard: No formal standard; practice measured against reduction within 6 hours and 12 hours of injury, based on published research

cycle1.result: Mean time to reduction 532 minutes (240–804); 4 (29%) reduced within 6 hours and 11 (79%) within 12 hours (abstract gives 28.6% and 71.4%). ED reductions (n=2) mean 275 minutes vs theatre (n=13) 576 minutes.

result.other_findings: Post-reduction neurovascular status documented in 100% and post-reduction CT in 87%; one AVN and one chondrolysis. Most Welsh EDs (20% with pathway) and UK MTCs (23% with pathway) lacked a pathway; a native hip dislocation ED pathway was introduced in February 2023 but not re-audited.

result.topic: Foot care provision in rheumatoid arthritis
result.setting: Rheumatology outpatient clinics, Counties Manukau District Health Board, Auckland
result.standard: Arthritis and Musculoskeletal Alliance (ARMA) Standards of Care for People with Foot Health Problems and Inflammatory Arthritis

cycle1.result: 77% reported no previous formal foot assessment; 76% had not seen a podiatrist; 40% had used the orthotic centre; 27% had previous foot surgery; over 85% had foot lesions.

result.other_findings: No patient had seen a podiatrist specialising in rheumatic disease, as the service only covered diabetes; many wore inappropriate open footwear (sandals 21%, mules 13%, jandals 10%). A specialist podiatrist within the rheumatology team was recommended.

result.setting: Bristol Royal Hospital for Children; tertiary paediatric hospital (paediatric medicine, surgery and orthopaedics)
result.standard: 17 admission documentation standards based on Royal College of Physicians clerking standards and RCPCH/PRSB digital record standards; aim to raise average compliance from 59% to above 90%

cycle1.result: Blank continuation sheets: 5 of 17 standards >90%, none 100%; medications 48%, allergies 47%, social history 36%, responsible consultant 8%, accompanying adult 24%, observations 38%.

result.intervention: Specialty-specific colour-coded pre-printed admission booklets with prompts and tick boxes (medicine, surgery, orthopaedics), introduced March 2019 with teaching at junior doctor handovers.

cycle2.dates: From March 2019 (first 40 booklet admissions per specialty)
cycle2.result: Average 33% absolute improvement (P < 0.01); 12 of 17 standards >90% and 4 at 100%; medications 99%, allergies 93%, consultant 88%, accompanying adult 68%, observations 52%.

result.other_findings: Observations (52%) and investigations (70%) remained poorly documented. Examination findings and plans were already well documented and changed little.

result.topic: Hip fracture orthogeriatric and preoperative medical assessment
result.setting: Chelsea & Westminster NHS Foundation Trust, London; district general hospital
result.standard: Cycle 1: Best Practice Tariff time to orthogeriatric assessment <72 hours and time to surgery <36 hours. Cycle 2: 100% preoperative medical assessment, orthogeriatric assessment <24 hours, time to surgery <36 hours

cycle1.result: Preoperative medical assessment 19%; mean time to orthogeriatric assessment 91 hours; mean time to surgery 37 hours; mean length of stay 24.8 days; inpatient mortality 14%.

result.intervention: New multidisciplinary hip fracture pathway from 1 June 2011: direct admission to the acute medical ward under joint named medical and orthopaedic consultants, anaesthetic assessment within 12 hours, consultant orthopaedic and orthogeriatric review within 24 hours; seminars and laminated posters for staff.

cycle2.result: Preoperative medical assessment 85% (p=0.0001); mean time to orthogeriatric assessment 19 hours (p=0.0001); mean time to surgery 31 hours (p=0.0663); length of stay 19.5 days (p=0.029); mortality 4% (p=0.0336).

result.other_findings: Return to original accommodation rose from 57% to 80% (p=0.0069), and delays over 36 hours due to inadequate medical optimisation fell from 41% to 17%. The main remaining cause of breaches was lack of morning trauma lists, since rescheduled.

result.topic: Oral nutritional supplementation after hip fracture
result.setting: 29 hospitals (24 Australian, 5 New Zealand) taking part in the ANZ Hip Fracture Registry Nutrition Sprint Audit
result.standard: ESPEN guideline and ANZ Hip Fracture Clinical Care Standard: all older adults with hip fracture should be offered oral nutritional supplements regardless of nutritional status

cycle1.result: ONS provided or prescribed for 182/385 (47.3%) of older adults having hip fracture surgery. ONS was more likely if malnourished on formal testing (OR 11.92; 95% CI 6.57, 21.69).

result.other_findings: ONS was also more likely with no preoperative medical assessment (OR 2.26), cognitive impairment (OR 1.83) and severe frailty or terminal illness (OR 3.17); New Zealand patients were less likely to receive ONS (OR 0.45). 30.9% of patients were diagnosed as malnourished.

result.setting: Two centres of one trauma and orthopaedic service (Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust / North Manchester General Hospital), knee arthroscopy day cases
result.standard: Correct ICD-10 and OPCS-4 coding of arthroscopic knee procedures from the operation note; proforma based on Royal College guidance for operation notes

cycle1.result: 17/34 (50%) cases coded incorrectly; tariff value £85,026 as coded versus £114,351 after correction, a loss of £29,325.

result.intervention: New coding-friendly knee arthroscopy operation note proforma with tick boxes, developed with coding staff and agreed at a consensus meeting, disseminated by email, notice boards and governance meetings.

cycle2.result: 2/37 (5%) cases coded incorrectly; £86,886 as coded versus £89,540 after correction, a loss of £2654.

result.other_findings: Most coding errors came from vague documentation of preoperative diagnoses and additional procedures (e.g. extra meniscectomy or cartilage debridement). Uptake of the proforma was slow and some cases were excluded for incorrect use of the form.

result.setting: Elective orthopaedic theatre lists (excluding spine and trauma), William Harvey Hospital, Ashford
result.standard: No existing standard; locally defined datapoints (surgical team, anaesthesia type, side, prosthesis/equipment, fluoroscopy, acronyms, extra patient information), later adopted as the 'William Harvey theatre list standard'

cycle1.result: 115 lists, 326 cases. Consultant in charge recorded in 85%; lead anaesthetist missing in 4.3%; 98% listed as GA (spinal 0.3%); 76.8% had no prosthesis/equipment detail; fluoroscopy requirement stated in 11% of cases needing it; acronyms used in 28%; extra patient information in 6%.

result.intervention: Proforma of essential information for waiting list coordinators, minor IT changes to the theatre list input form, and education of waiting list coordinators and trainees.

cycle2.result: 100 lists, 255 cases. Consultant in charge recorded in 100%; 80% listed as GA (14.5% spinal per abstract; 37 regional); no prosthesis/equipment detail fell to 43% (abstract: prosthesis/equipment mentioned 34% vs 23%); fluoroscopy stated in 25% of cases needing it; acronyms 6%; extra patient information 49.8%.

result.other_findings: Lead anaesthetist was missing in 16% of lists at re-audit (worse than 4.3%), and only 5.3% of hip arthroplasty cases stated cement requirement in both rounds. A staff questionnaire (38/40 completed) informed the datapoints.

result.topic: Ankle fracture management in older adults
result.setting: Bristol Royal Infirmary, patients aged 50 to 80 admitted with ankle fractures
result.standard: No best-practice standard stated for management; DEXA scanning in patients over 65 compared with NICE (2011) osteoporosis recommendations

cycle1.result: 42 (84%) operative and 8 (16%) non-operative. Malunion (63%) and failed fixation (25%) more common after non-operative care. Formal bone protection strategy in 3 patients (6%); only 3 patients (14%) aged over 65 had a DEXA scan.

result.other_findings: Malunion and failed fixation were significantly higher after surgery without consultant supervision (p = 0.043). Recommendations were DEXA for all over 65s and consultant supervision for bi- and trimalleolar fixation; re-audit was outside the project scope.

result.setting: District general hospital emergency department and associated nurse-led Minor Injury Unit, Mid and South Essex NHS Trust (Basildon)
result.standard: NICE NG38: non-rigid immobilisation (removable splint or bandage) and discharge without routine follow-up for distal radius torus fractures; target 100%

cycle1.result: Compliance 97/174 (56%) at DGH and 0/48 (0%) at MIU, combined 97/222 (44%). Rigid immobilisation 77/174 (44%) DGH and 48/48 (100%) MIU. Fracture clinic follow-up 128/222 (58%).

result.intervention: Educational posters in ED and MIU, NG38 emailed to all clinical staff, teaching sessions (two at DGH, one at MIU) and reinforcement at governance meetings (October 2023 to February 2024).

cycle2.result: Compliance 131/164 (80%) at DGH (p < 0.001) and 29/94 (31%) at MIU (p < 0.001), combined 160/258 (62%). Fracture clinic follow-up 98/258 (38%) (p < 0.001).

result.other_findings: Rigid immobilisation persisted in 33/164 (20%) at DGH and 65/94 (69%) at MIU; splint stock at the MIU may have contributed. No balancing measures were collected.

result.setting: Orthopaedic trauma ward, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (major trauma centre)
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians Health Informatics Unit 2019 discharge summary content standards

cycle1.result: Follow-up plan fully detailed 15.6% (5/32); new medication indication documented 9.4% (3/32); patient advice fully detailed 21.2% (7/33); inpatient management fully detailed 30.3% (10/33).

result.intervention: Educational poster with a checklist of RCP components, interactive teaching sessions, a discharge summary self-assessment checklist, reminders with one-to-one feedback for junior doctors and a team campaign (August to September 2025).

cycle2.result: Follow-up plan fully detailed 90.0% (18/20) (p < 0.0001); new medication indication 50.0% (9/18) (p = 0.004); patient advice fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.0002); inpatient management fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.001).

result.other_findings: Any safety-net advice fell from 96.9% (32/33) to 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.02), though when present it was more often excellent. Seven-day readmission was 6.1% vs 4.8%, with no change.

result.setting: Single-centre MRI service (QLD X-ray, QEII Hospital, Brisbane), 3T scanner
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 31 patients (32 knees). DIXON images judged comparable replacements for sagittal PD and PD fat-saturated sequences with no loss of diagnostic confidence; reviewer 1 mean image quality 1.56 and fat suppression 1.19; scan time saving just over 10% (about 1 minute per patient).

result.other_findings: Patient motion affected 5 series (15.6%) and a minor chemical shift artefact was seen at the femoral cartilage, neither affecting diagnosis.

result.topic: Hip fracture operation choice per NICE guidance
result.setting: Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge (major trauma centre), patients over 65 having hip fracture surgery
result.standard: NICE CG124 Section 1.6 (choice of arthroplasty, THR for eligible displaced intracapsular fractures, extramedullary implants for A1/A2 trochanteric fractures, intramedullary nail for subtrochanteric fractures)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 76.04% (1244/1636). THR documented as considered in 43.6% (193/443) of eligible patients; 56.43% of THR-indicated patients had no documented consideration (65.41% in 2020).

result.intervention: A 'smart phrase' NICE THR-eligibility checklist added to the electronic (Epic) neck of femur clerking proforma in June 2021.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 87.43% (459/525) (z = 5.556, p < 0.01). THR considered in 57.89% (77/133); 42.11% of THR-indicated patients lacked documented consideration (z = 2.904, p < 0.01).

result.other_findings: The proportion of patients actually receiving THR did not increase, and use of the smart phrase declined over time without a drop in compliance. NICE CG124 changed in January 2023, making the smart phrase outdated.

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Prince Osman Digna Referral Hospital, Port Sudan (tertiary referral centre), handwritten notes
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice: 18 core operation note criteria

cycle1.dates: not reported (audit ran May 2024 to May 2025)
cycle1.result: Anticipated blood loss, antibiotic prophylaxis and DVT prophylaxis each 0/50 (0%); operative findings 17/50 (34%); tissue removed/altered 16/50 (32%); surgical approach 20/50 (40%); surgeon name 49/50 (98%).

result.intervention: Presentation of findings at a governance meeting, distribution and discussion of RCS operation note standards, and senior-led feedback and reinforcement in theatre.

cycle2.result: Anticipated blood loss 10/35 (28.6%); antibiotic prophylaxis 7/35 (20%); DVT prophylaxis 5/35 (14.3%); operative findings 26/35 (74.3%); tissue altered 25/35 (71.4%); surgical approach 28/35 (80%); surgeon name 35/35 (100%).

result.other_findings: Elective/emergency status stayed poor at 11/35 (31.4%) and surgeon signature was 30/35 (85.7%). The authors recommend a mandatory operation note template.

result.setting: District general hospital, patients aged 60 or over with neck of femur fracture who had pre-operative TTE
result.standard: Local trust guideline: no surgical delay awaiting echo; TTE only for listed indications; all TTE reports acknowledged by the anaesthetist; target 100%

cycle1.result: No surgical delay 12/12 (100%); appropriate requests 4/12 (33.3%); reports acknowledged by anaesthetist 10/12 (83.3%).

result.intervention: Teaching sessions, posters of request criteria, dissemination of audit findings, reminders at safety meetings and printed prompt cards.

cycle2.result: No surgical delay 17/17 (100%); appropriate requests 16/17 (94.1%); reports acknowledged 12/17 (70.6%).

result.other_findings: Acknowledgement of echo reports fell. TTE findings changed anaesthetic management in 4/17 (23.5%), mainly invasive arterial monitoring.

result.setting: Nine NHS hospitals across six university health boards in Wales, trainee collaborative (WORC) prospective snapshot audit
result.standard: BOAST guideline on management of ankle fractures (documentation, imaging including CT for posterior malleolus, weight-bearing X-rays, early weight-bearing)

cycle1.result: Documentation: mechanism 94.4%, skin 71.3%, neurovascular status 80.1%, comorbidities 81%, alcohol 34.3%, smoking 41.7%. Mortice view 75.9%. CT for posterior malleolus fracture 15/31 (48.38%) operative and 0/9 non-operative. Weight-bearing X-ray in non-operative group 22/106 (20.8%). Early weight-bearing 63/106 (59.43%) non-operative and 11/110 (10%) operative.

result.other_findings: Reason for delayed weight-bearing after surgery was documented in only 16/99 (16.16%). Education, an infographic and a re-audit were planned.

result.topic: Ottawa ankle and knee rules compliance
result.setting: Emergency department and urgent treatment centre, Lincoln County Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: Ottawa Ankle and Knee Rules (incorporated in NICE guidance) for requesting X-rays

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 59.5%; knee X-rays 74.6% (n=182); ankle X-rays 33.1% (n=46). Positivity 18.0% knee and 32.0% ankle.

result.intervention: Educational session, leaflets, posters in ED and UTC and emails to clinicians (August 2023).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 85% (221/260); knee X-rays 89.9% (152); ankle X-rays 75.8% (69). Positivity 18.9% knee and 44.0% ankle.

result.other_findings: Compliance was much lower for patients under 55 (22.5% in cycle 1, 69.9% in cycle 2). Compliance was judged from radiology requests only.

result.setting: Regional referral hospitals in Cameroon (Delphi panel of surgeons and interviews at three facilities)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Panel of 7 surgeons: 23 of 40 audit filter variables met consensus and 21 had median score of 4 or more (e.g. vitals, breathing assessment and two large-bore IVs within 15 min; IV antimicrobials within 1 h for open fractures). 16 providers interviewed.

result.other_findings: Barriers were limited staff and materials and patients' inability to pay; regular trauma training and staff buy-in were seen as promoters.

result.topic: Accuracy of emergency department fracture clinic referrals
result.setting: Acute orthopaedic (fracture) clinic receiving Accident and Emergency referrals, Yorkshire Regional Health Authority
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 17.2% had an incorrect diagnosis and 12% had been incorrectly treated; 49.4% of plaster splints were removed and 25.4% substantially altered; 6% admitted from clinic.

result.other_findings: Authors argue for audit and direct feedback to A&E staff to improve care and use of resources.

result.topic: Labelling of fluids in the sterile field
result.setting: Orthopaedic department (three orthopaedic theatres, two elective and one trauma) of a district general hospital
result.standard: Royal Pharmaceutical Society and Royal College of Anaesthetists guidelines: all syringes/containers of fluid in the sterile field labelled with fluid name and concentration

cycle1.result: 3/30 procedures (10%) compliant with labelling guidelines; labelling information adequate in only 1 of these 3

result.intervention: Sterile stickers with surgical marker pens for labelling by the scrub nurse, a mandatory 'tactical pause and check' after opening sets, and an awareness campaign (posters, emails, educational sessions)

cycle2.result: 32/34 procedures (94%) compliant (p<0.00001, Fisher's exact test); labelling adequate in 28 of labelled cases

result.other_findings: Baseline reasons for non-compliance were lack of sterile labels, inconvenience at critical moments and human factors. In cycle 2, 3/34 fluids were not labelled immediately after drawing up.

result.topic: Ottawa knee rules compliance for knee radiographs
result.setting: Emergency department, St. Luke's General Hospital, Kilkenny (general hospital)
result.standard: RCR iRefer guidelines: ≥95% of knee radiographs requested in accordance with Ottawa Knee Rules; ≥95% of requests documenting an OKR indication; unnecessary imaging ≤10%

cycle1.result: OKR compliance 50 (72.5%); non-compliant requests 19 (27.5%); documentation of suspected fracture/bone injury 23 (32.9%); negative X-rays 37 (52.9%)

result.intervention: Interactive teaching session for ED clinicians, OKR leaflets distributed and emailed, and posters in ED clinical areas and beside imaging request stations

cycle2.result: OKR compliance 66 (83.5%) (χ²=2.05, p=0.15); non-compliant requests 13 (16.5%); documentation of suspected fracture/bone injury 44 (55.7%) (p=0.01); negative X-rays 30 (38.0%) (p=0.08)

result.other_findings: Compliance remained below the 95% target. Estimated radiographer time saved was about 60-90 minutes per cycle.

result.topic: Hip fracture best practice tariff and mortality
result.setting: St Peter's Hospital, Ashford & St Peter's NHS Trust, orthogeriatric hip fracture service
result.standard: Blue Book standards and hip fracture best practice tariff (including time to theatre within 36 hours), tracked via NHFD

cycle1.result: 39.6% operated within 36 hours (2010); best practice tariff attainment 28% (2010); 30-day mortality 7.8%

result.intervention: Integrated orthogeriatricians; LEAN (EQuIP) pathway redesign with split weekend theatre lists, priority theatre pyramid, new clerking proforma with falls and bone health, A-Z preoperative guide, fast bleep, extra pressure mattresses, seven-day physiotherapy, monthly governance meetings, and measures to prevent post-operative complications and improve Wednesday-admission review

cycle2.result: 84% operated within 36 hours (national 71%); best practice tariff attainment 83% (national 55%); 30-day mortality 5.3% (national 8.2%)

result.other_findings: Peak results in 2012 were 88% within 36 hours and 88% BPT. Pressure ulcers fell from 5.4% to 3.2%, mobilisation within 24 hours rose from 41% to 75%, and Wednesday-admission mortality fell from 9.2% to 1.69%.

result.setting: Orthopaedic Surgery Department, Gezira Traumatology Center, Wad Madani Teaching Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons Good Surgical Practice operative note guidance (14 parameters)

cycle1.result: Mean compliance 82.0%; theatre anaesthetist name 1 (4.3%), anticipated blood loss 3 (13%), antibiotic prophylaxis 2 (8.7%), complications 12 (52.2%); procedure 22 (95.7%) and signature 23 (100%)

result.intervention: Staff education, a standardised RCS-aligned operative note template, posters in theatres and staff areas, and a senior feedback mechanism

cycle2.result: Mean compliance 83.4%; anaesthetist name 19 (82.6%), anticipated blood loss 19 (82.6%), antibiotic prophylaxis 16 (69.6%), complications 21 (91.3%)

result.other_findings: Prosthesis identification fell from 20 (87%) to 6 (26.1%) and tissue details from 20 (87%) to 15 (65.2%); incision and closure documentation also declined.

result.topic: Suspected cauda equina syndrome MRI waiting time
result.setting: Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, a district general hospital with no on-site spinal services; trauma and orthopaedic referrals from the emergency department
result.standard: NICE, BASS and SBNS guidelines and local trust protocol; National Suspected CES Pathway recommends MRI within four hours of request

cycle1.result: Mean MRI waiting time 12.5 hours (8am-4pm 9.5 h; 4pm-12am 18 h; 12am-8am 8.5 h); same-day discharge 27 (29%); inpatient stay 66 (71%)

result.intervention: Introduction of a middle-grade trauma and orthopaedic doctor in the emergency department (urgent treatment centre) to assess suspected CES patients

cycle2.result: Mean MRI waiting time 8 hours (8am-4pm 5.5 h; 4pm-12am 13 h; 12am-8am 6.5 h); all MRI scans and reports within 24 hours; same-day discharge 21 (58%); inpatient stay 15 (42%)

result.other_findings: No patient in cycle 2 had confirmed CES (possible CES in 1, 3%). Admissions fell from an average of 11 to 7 patients per month.

result.topic: Fascia iliaca block for hip fracture
result.setting: District hospital (Salisbury), emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics; NHFD data
result.standard: NICE hip fracture guidance and BOAST fragility fracture analgesia guidance; local decision that all hip fracture patients receive FICB on presentation unless contraindicated

cycle1.result: FICB administered in 45 (24.5%); mean post-FICB pain score 4 (NRS)

result.intervention: Results discussed at departmental and Trust mortality meetings, one-to-one teaching on loss-of-resistance FICB for ED and T&O junior doctors, and enforcing completion of the hip fracture clinical proforma with FICB sign-off or documented contraindication

cycle2.result: FICB administered in 94 (44.3%) (p<0.00001); mean post-FICB pain score 3.6 (p<0.0011)

result.other_findings: The text gives 148 patients in the first audit but the table gives n=184. No FICB complications were recorded; block success rate was 74%.

result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Department, University Hospital of North Tees; elective hip arthroplasty operative notes
result.standard: GIRFT, British Hip Society and BOA July 2019 total hip arthroplasty best practice guidance (24 documentation criteria)

cycle1.result: Handwritten notes scored an average of 12/24 (50%); compliance ranged 0%-100% across criteria, e.g. protection of critical structures 15%, leg length/neurovascular status 20%, intraoperative complications 5%; 80% legible

result.intervention: Pre-populated GIRFT-compliant online hip arthroplasty operative note proforma in the local 'Trackcare' electronic system, typed notes

cycle2.result: Typed notes with the computerised proforma scored an average of 22/24 (92%) (p<0.05); compliance 80%-100% across criteria; 15 of 24 criteria significantly improved; 100% legible

result.other_findings: 25 handwritten notes were collected in cycle 1 and 5 illegible notes excluded. Anaesthetist name and grade stayed at 80%; average documentation time fell from 25 to 7 minutes.

result.setting: Eight NHS community podiatry departments in the Trent and South Yorkshire region
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Podiatry Health Questionnaire score improved from mean 11.8 to 11.2 and pain VAS from 4.8 to 4.1 two weeks after treatment (p<0.0001); 75% of patients stayed the same or improved

result.other_findings: Before-and-after outcome audit with no standard; 25% of patients reported worse scores after treatment and the improvements were small.

result.topic: Complications of minimally invasive lesser toe surgery
result.setting: Single surgeon's practice, procedures in office procedure rooms and hospitals/surgi-centres on a day-case basis
result.standard: Australasian College of Podiatric Surgeons surgical audit clinical indicators (developed from the ACHS clinical indicator program); compared with published complication rates for open digital surgery

cycle1.result: 299 digits operated on; 1 superficial infection (0.56%), 2 under-corrections needing revision (0.67%); no other ACPS indicator events, no neurovascular or medical complications

result.other_findings: Two patients (0.7%) had pain from delayed union at 4 months that resolved by 6 months. 45% of procedures were done in an office setting without fluoroscopy.

result.setting: Tertiary referral hospital, Clinical Center Nis
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Plate (n=36) versus IM nail (n=20): union 100% versus 90%; mean Constant-Murley score 82.40 versus 77.58 (p=0.246); complications 13.8% versus 10%

result.other_findings: Retrospective comparative outcome study; IM nailing had significantly lower blood loss, shorter surgery and shorter hospital stay (all p<0.001).

result.setting: Emergency department and trauma unit, The Grange University Hospital, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
result.standard: Health board clinical pathway for traumatic anterior shoulder instability, aligned with BOA and BESS guidance (pre- and post-reduction radiographs, neurovascular assessment, specialist follow-up)

cycle1.result: Pre- and post-reduction radiographs in 97/100 (97%), post-reduction only in 3 (3%); MUA successful in 98 (98%); mean time to reduction 152 minutes; nerve injury in 28 (28%)

result.other_findings: Not all patients under 40 received an MR arthrogram as recommended. Posterior dislocations made up 16% of cases and 10 patients were lost to follow-up.

result.topic: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
result.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery, University Hospital Waterford (regional trauma centre), day-case trauma lists
result.standard: BOAST distal radius fracture guidance: intra-articular fractures operated within 72 hours and extra-articular within seven days; local target ≥80%

cycle1.result: Intra-articular within 3 days of injury 16/27 (59%); extra-articular within 7 days of injury 24/26 (92%); intra-articular within 3 days of referral 20/27 (74%)

result.intervention: Staff education on BOAST guidance for doctors and trauma coordinators at the morbidity and mortality meeting (PDSA 1), then repeat education and changing the trauma list spreadsheet dropdown to separate intra-articular and extra-articular distal radius fractures (PDSA 2)

cycle2.result: Intra-articular within 3 days of injury 24/32 (75%) (p=0.2665; p trend=0.1924); extra-articular within 7 days of injury 13/19 (68%) (p=0.0119; p trend=0.0243); intra-articular within 3 days of referral 28/32 (88%)

result.other_findings: Second cycle (April to June 2024, n=57): intra-articular within 3 days of injury 14/25 (56%) and extra-articular within 7 days 31/32 (97%). Intra-articular timeliness stayed below the 80% target and extra-articular timeliness fell in the final cycle.

result.setting: Orthopaedics department, MVJ Medical College and Research Hospital, tertiary care hospital, Bangalore
result.standard: Standard discharge summary checklist from a systematic review (predetermined set of criteria)

cycle1.dates: Audited between May 22 and October 22 (handwritten summaries, before electronic summaries introduced on 8 January 2022)
cycle1.result: Handwritten summaries: complications in hospital 50%, contact information 34%, condition at discharge 66%, understandability 58%, allergies 66%, problem list/issues pending 35%, discharge medications 88%, follow-up plan 80%; patient signature 0%

result.intervention: Introduction of electronic discharge summaries using a standardised form completed by orthopaedic residents (from 8 January 2022)

cycle2.result: Electronic summaries: complications in hospital 100%, contact information 95%, condition at discharge 96%, understandability 100%, allergies 100%, problem list/issues pending 92%, discharge medications 100%, follow-up plan 100%; patient signature 100%

result.other_findings: Social issues, cultural concepts, support to relatives, palliative care information, discharge destination, clinical trial involvement and sick note were documented in 0% of both handwritten and electronic summaries. No statistical testing was done.

result.setting: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, Stanmore; senior registrar appointments
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Abstract only: analysis of the CVs of 50 trainees appointed as senior registrars to identify the normal pattern of educational achievement.

result.topic: Supracondylar fracture lateral pin fixation stability
result.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic departments, Hallym Sacred Heart, Haeundae Paik and Severance Children's hospitals (retrospective review)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Retrospective risk-factor study of lateral-only pinning for Gartland type III fractures; medial comminution in 20 patients (29.8%); pin separation lower with medial comminution (33.8% vs 38.1%, P=0.017); medial comminution associated with Baumann angle change (OR 4.151, 95% CI 1.249–13.800, P=0.020).

result.other_findings: No iatrogenic ulnar nerve injury; all Baumann angle differences were under 10°. Authors recommend an additional medial pin when medial comminution is present.

result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Kettering General Hospital
result.standard: BOA-endorsed consent guidance (orthoconsent.com); departmental standard of 100% documentation of common, less common and rare risks on Consent Form 1 for NOF fracture surgery

cycle1.result: 2015 cycle: infection 100%, bleeding 87%, clots 93%, anaesthetic risks 53%, neurovascular injury 93%, pain 73%, altered wound healing 60%, non/mal-union 33%, failure of surgery 87%, mortality 40%, prosthetic dislocation 0%, leg length discrepancy 0%.

result.intervention: Verbal and written dissemination of results, printed risk list displayed in the orthopaedic doctors' office, and amendments to the junior doctor induction handbook.
