cycle2.result: Of 100 NOF patients, 48 with capacity (AMT ≥8) audited: infection, bleeding, clots and anaesthetic risks 100%; neurovascular injury 98%; failure of surgery 83%; pain 75%; non/mal-union 71%; altered wound healing 69%; mortality 21%; prosthetic dislocation 14%; leg length discrepancy 6%.

result.other_findings: Three cycles (2015, 2016, 2019); 2016 values included anaesthetic risks 76%, pain 42% and mortality 61%. The 100% target was still not met; after the latest cycle the trust approved two consent-specific stickers (arthroplasty/fixation) and inappropriate abbreviations were noted.

result.setting: Trauma unit, district general hospital, University Hospitals Dorset (Poole)
result.standard: BOAST ankle fracture guidance; radiological evidence of intra-operative syndesmosis stress testing saved and documented on operation notes, target 80% each

cycle1.result: Radiological evidence saved 55% (n=49); documentation on operation notes 71% (n=63); neither in 25% (n=22).

result.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance; poster in on-call room and theatre areas and a teaching presentation by an associate specialist foot and ankle surgeon.

cycle2.result: Radiological evidence saved 82% (n=41), p=0.001; documentation 82% (n=41), p=0.14; neither in 6% (n=3). Both targets met.

result.other_findings: Audit did not assess the quality or technique of the stress tests, only their presence.

result.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis in hip fracture arthroplasty
result.setting: Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust guideline: three postoperative IV doses of flucloxacillin (teicoplanin if penicillin allergic) after hip arthroplasty for NOF fracture; target 100%

cycle1.result: Postoperative antibiotics given to 150/179 (83.8%), none to 29 (16.2%); 84/121 (69.4%) flucloxacillin recipients completed all three doses; 97/179 (54.2%) fully compliant overall.

result.other_findings: Of 29 with no antibiotics, 12 were mentioned in notes but not prescribed, 8 recorded as not required and 9 not mentioned. Three superficial wound infections (1.7%) and no PJI.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic unit, Monklands District General Hospital, NHS Lanarkshire (emergency admissions)
result.standard: SIGN guideline 122 VTE prophylaxis; seven-item checklist (weight/BMI and eGFR recorded, correct LMWH dose, timely administration, AES prescribed and worn, early mobilisation, hydration), 100% target

cycle1.result: 71% of patients compliant with all measures; errors mainly medical (failure to prescribe LMWH or stockings, incorrect dosing), plus nursing and patient errors; about 30% of surveyed patients (n=47) understood aims of VTE prophylaxis.

result.intervention: Policy of prophylaxis unless contraindicated, summarised guidelines displayed on wards, MDT teaching for doctors and nurses, patient education, VTE added to handover and radiology meeting, teaching after rota change, and VTE education added to junior doctor induction.

cycle2.result: Re-audit 4: 100% compliance; 80% of patients understood aims of VTE prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: Re-audits: 93% (n=27), 100% (n=26), 86% (n=22, dip after medical staff rotation), 100% (n=25); spot audit six months later showed 100%.

result.topic: Preoperative templating radiographs for hip arthroplasty
result.setting: Elective arthroplasty service, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Templating radiographs 7–180 days before THA (New Zealand Orthopaedic Association, South African Arthroplasty Society and GIRFT guidance); goal 100%

cycle1.result: 10/50 (20%) had templating radiographs within 7–180 days; mean 140 days (range 0–788) from latest radiograph to surgery.

result.intervention: Departmental protocol requiring preoperative assessment with templating radiographs, education of NCHDs on radiographs to order, and a departmental rota assigning NCHDs to order them.
result.other_findings: Mean leg length change of 2.26 mm (range 0–17 mm) between radiographs a mean 386 days apart.

result.topic: Paediatric distal forearm fracture ED manipulation (BOAST)
result.setting: Emergency department, district general hospital with paediatric orthopaedic services, Gloucestershire Royal Hospital
result.standard: BOAST early management of distal forearm fractures in children (May 2021): early ED manipulation, neurovascular and consent documentation, orthogonal X-rays, fracture clinic within 7 days

cycle1.result: 23/72 (31.94%) manipulated in ED; 11 of 23 ED manipulations failed.

result.intervention: Local trust pathway in line with BOAST introduced from July 2021 (analgesia/sedation, location, manipulation and referral guidance) with staff education.

cycle2.result: 73/87 manipulated in ED (p<0.00001); 63 (86.31%) acceptable reduction, 10 (13.69%) failed. BOAST compliance: neurovascular documentation pre-manipulation 93.10% (81/87), before discharge 64.36% (56/87); consent documentation 73.56% (64/87); orthogonal X-rays 100% (87/87); fracture clinic within 7 days 49.42% (43/87), mean 8.25 days.

result.other_findings: Reasons for not attempting ED manipulation (14 cases) were not documented; about 63 hours of theatre time saved. Protocol changed so off-ended fractures are manipulated under sedation.

result.setting: Single centre orthopaedic and radiology departments (Leeds Teaching Hospitals affiliation)
result.standard: Local consensus criteria (seven arthroplasty and three radiology consultants): nine criteria for adequate post-operative hip and knee arthroplasty radiographs, four essential

cycle1.result: 69/100 radiographs adequate overall; whole prosthesis and cement visible 86%, relevant anatomy visible 83%, pubic symphysis centred 31%, GT/LT level 32%.

result.intervention: Local guidelines published with radiology, educational and feedback meetings with radiographers, poster in radiography rooms and a quality improvement proforma.

cycle2.result: 84/100 adequate overall; prosthesis and cement visible 93%, relevant anatomy 95%, pubic symphysis centred 47%, GT/LT level 43%; 11/56 (19.6%) hip and 5/44 (11.4%) knee radiographs inadequate.

result.other_findings: Pain score, BMI and number of radiographers were not correlated with inadequate radiographs; exposure fell slightly (95% to 92%).

result.setting: Plastic surgery acute referrals (OARS), Oxford University Hospitals NHS teaching trust
result.standard: BSSH Hand Trauma App guidance and local OUH guidelines on indications for antibiotics in open hand injuries

cycle1.result: 22/44 (50.0%) referrals without an indication were given or advised antibiotics; 10/84 (12%) with an indication were neither given nor advised antibiotics.

result.intervention: Infographic poster displayed and emailed to resident doctors (PDSA 1), then a short microlearning video shared on WhatsApp and email (PDSA 2).

cycle2.result: 5/35 (14.3%) without an indication given or advised antibiotics (p=0.002 vs baseline).

result.other_findings: After the infographic alone (25/7/22–31/7/22, n=52), 7/16 (43.8%) were given unnecessary antibiotics (not significant). Three of the five remaining cases were given antibiotics by the referrer before referral.

result.setting: Tertiary elective orthopaedic hospital, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, London
result.standard: NICE VTE guideline (over 16s): VTE risk reassessment within 24 hours after surgery; target 100%

cycle1.result: 6/4780 (0.13%) had VTE reassessment completed within 24 hours of surgery.

result.intervention: Automated system prompt on EPMA reminding staff to complete VTE reassessment 24 hours after surgery.

cycle2.result: 112/156 (74%) completed within 24 hours (p<0.0001); 131/156 (83%) completed at any time.

result.other_findings: Initial VTE assessment compliance was high because it is a mandatory step on EPMA.

result.setting: East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE hip fracture guidance: sliding hip screw for 31A1/A2 fractures, intramedullary nail for 31A3 and reverse oblique fractures

cycle1.result: Compliance with national guidance on appropriate operation 63% (n=33/52) initially, 73% (n=38/52) after senior review of coding and classification; days to discharge from therapies 8.4 (short nail) vs 11 (DHS), P=0.03.

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality 13% (7/52) overall, higher than the national 5.5%; operating time similar (58.11 vs 58.03 min).

result.setting: Level one trauma centre, trauma and orthopaedics department (Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast affiliation)
result.standard: GMC, RCS Glasgow and BOA consent guidance; no abbreviations on consent forms

cycle1.result: Abbreviations in 189/350 (54%) forms; mostly by registrars (74%); DVT and PE commonest.

result.intervention: Results presented at M&M meeting, email to all staff, reminder sticker attached to consent forms and poster in areas where consent is taken.
result.other_findings: DVT and PE remained the commonest abbreviations; use of CRPS, PIP and EUA rose in proportion.

result.setting: 28 UK hospitals (district general, major trauma and teaching centres)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Descriptive service evaluation: 50% of injuries considered preventable; commonest injuries single phalanx fracture (15%), wrist fracture (15%), single metacarpal fracture (13%).

result.other_findings: Collected during COVID-19 lockdown; alcohol linked to 1.9% and drugs to 0.54% of injuries.

result.topic: Next of kin involvement in consent for patients lacking capacity
result.setting: 520-bed district general hospital trauma unit (Royal Surrey County Hospital)
result.standard: Mental Capacity Act 2005 best-interests process; documented attempt to contact next of kin before surgery and completion of NoK section of Consent Form Four

cycle1.result: Documented attempt to contact NoK 80% (24/30); NoK section of Consent Form Four completed 30% (10/30).

result.intervention: Feedback presentation at trauma meeting and email to orthopaedic team.

cycle2.result: Documented attempt to contact NoK 100% (28/28), p<0.05; NoK section completed 64.3% (18/28), p<0.05.

result.other_findings: Registrar survey suggested the Consent Form Four NoK section is easily missed; planned consent e-training and form redesign.

result.topic: Ileus after pelvic and acetabular fractures
result.setting: Major Trauma Unit, Royal Victoria Hospital, Belfast (Major Trauma Centre)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Clinically significant ileus 4.12% (4/97); 80.4% (78/97) failed to achieve GI-2 by day 3, mostly due to constipation.

result.other_findings: Length of stay correlated with time to bowel opening (r=0.498, p<0.001); constipation associated with 6.5 days longer stay.

result.topic: Hip fracture early mobilisation and physiotherapy
result.setting: Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother Hospital, Margate, Kent; main orthopaedic ward and outlier wards
result.standard: National guidelines (NICE): mobilisation on the day of or the day after hip fracture surgery; two hours of physiotherapy in the first week after surgery; no target stated

cycle1.result: 93% (106/113) seen by a physiotherapist on the day of or day after surgery (main orthopaedic ward 94%, 80/85; outliers 93%, 21/28; P=0.3). 40% (46/113) had delayed mobilisation. 83% (94/113) had two hours of physiotherapy in the first week. Clear documentation of mobilisation in 85% (97/113).

result.other_findings: Reasons for delayed mobilisation: post-operative delirium 32.6% (15/46), low haemoglobin 26% (12/46), pain 21.7% (10/46), dementia 4.3% (2/46), no documented reason 15.2% (7/46). Presence of one or more of these factors was associated with one-year mortality of 25.8% (16/62, P=0.05), with delirium the strongest single factor (P=0.01).

result.topic: Neurovascular assessment documentation in limb fractures
result.setting: Tertiary care hospital / major trauma centre; emergency department and orthopaedic clerking of patients admitted to trauma wards with acute fractures
result.standard: British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) on documentation of neurovascular assessment; no target stated

cycle1.result: ED notes: no neurovascular documentation 17 (22.1%), 'NVI' only 30 (38.9%), specific documentation 30 (38.9%). Orthopaedic notes: no documentation 3 (3.8%), NVI only 16 (20.7%), specific documentation 58 (75.3%). Post-manipulation in ED (n=19): no documentation 12 (63.2%), specific 6 (31.6%).

result.intervention: Posters in trauma units, generic educational emails to all ED and orthopaedic doctors, and consultant-led joint ED and orthopaedic teaching sessions.

cycle2.result: ED notes: no documentation 6 (7.3%), NVI only 8 (9.7%), specific documentation 68 (82.9%). Orthopaedic notes: no documentation 0 (0%), NVI only 4 (3.6%), specific documentation 74 (90.2%). Post-manipulation in ED (n=22): no documentation 7 (31.8%), NVI only 4 (18.1%), specific 11 (50%).

result.other_findings: Post-manipulation neurovascular documentation remained poor, with nearly a third of manipulated patients still having none. Patients clerked by the project authors were excluded from the re-audit.

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis after ankle fracture surgery
result.setting: Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust, single centre, operatively managed ankle fractures
result.standard: NICE guidance on pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for ankle surgery with immobilisation, and BOAST requirement that VTE prophylaxis follows agreed local protocols; no target stated

cycle1.result: Operation note documentation of VTE chemoprophylaxis: agent and duration specified 40 (29%), nonspecific 40 (29%), none 57 (42%). Discharged with VTE chemoprophylaxis 78 (57%).

result.intervention: Quality Improvement Half-Day educating surgeons and ward junior doctors; new written local policy of enoxaparin 40 mg once daily for 6 weeks for all operatively managed ankle fractures unless contraindicated; posters for 3 weeks in theatre and ward areas; review of prophylaxis at 2- and 6-week clinics.

cycle2.result: Operation note agent and duration specified 44 (90%), nonspecific 3 (6%), none 2 (4%) (all P<0.001). Discharged with VTE chemoprophylaxis 48 (98%) (P<0.001).

result.other_findings: In cycle 1, discharge prophylaxis was 97.2% when agent and duration were in the operation note versus 51.8% with nonspecific and 32.4% with no documentation (P<0.001). Two VTE events (one DVT, one PE) occurred in cycle 1 and none in cycle 2.

result.setting: University teaching hospital and regional trauma and orthopaedic referral centre serving four peripheral sites (Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda, per affiliation); non-operative fracture pathway
result.standard: Three modified BOASTs: early senior review (BOAST: new fracture clinic within 72 hours; measured as VFC review within 24 hours), minimising outpatient visits, and patient-initiated follow-up as the default; no target stated

cycle1.result: 39% of non-operative patients triaged to the VFC within 24 hours; 61% sent directly to face-to-face clinic. 35,399 face-to-face fracture clinic appointments (also given as 35,339 in the results).

result.intervention: COVID-19-era policy changes: mandatory VFC triage of all non-operative injuries via a smartphone referral app with daily consultant-led multidisciplinary review, and an early appropriate discharge / patient-initiated follow-up policy; national lockdowns also occurred.

cycle2.result: 100% of non-operative patients assessed in the VFC within 24 hours. Face-to-face appointments fell to 17,639, a 50.2% reduction: 3.7% attributed to national lockdowns, 14.7% to VFC triage and 35.5% to early appropriate discharge.

result.other_findings: Sample sizes are total orthopaedic referrals in each period. Patient safety and satisfaction were not assessed.

result.topic: Elective cancellations due to asymptomatic bacteriuria
result.setting: Lister Hospital, Stevenage (East & North Herts NHS Trust), large district general hospital offering tertiary orthopaedic services; cancelled elective orthopaedic operations
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Of 33 all-cause cancellations, 7 (21.2%) were cancelled for UTI risk on positive urinalysis; only 1 (14.3%) of these was symptomatic, so 6 (85.7%) were cancelled for asymptomatic bacteriuria.

result.intervention: New symptom-based protocol from 1 May 2019: all patients complete a 7-item UTI symptom questionnaire and surgery is cancelled only if two or more symptoms are reported, regardless of urinalysis.

cycle2.result: Of 45 all-cause cancellations, 2 (4.4%) were cancelled for UTI risk, both symptomatic; 4 (8.8%) had positive urinalysis, the 2 asymptomatic ones cancelled for unrelated reasons. No cancellations for asymptomatic bacteriuria; estimated 71.4% reduction in cancellations for UTI risk.

result.other_findings: Patients with positive urinalysis whose operations were not cancelled were not captured, so the true effect is estimated. Each cancelled operation was estimated to waste 2.1 hours of theatre time (about £2,525).

result.setting: Galway University Hospital, orthopaedic outpatient clinic letters
result.standard: Laterality (left or right) stated in the diagnosis in outpatient clinic letters; no named guideline or target stated

cycle1.dates: One week within February to August 2023
cycle1.result: Laterality mentioned in 65.1% of letters. By grade: SHO 78.8%, registrar 62.7%, consultant 54.3% (P<0.05).

result.intervention: Educational sessions on specifying laterality, reminder stickers placed in the clinic as visual prompts, and liaison with secretarial staff who transcribe dictated letters.
result.other_findings: Consultants had the lowest rate of stating laterality at baseline. Re-audit analysed the same number of letters over one week.

result.topic: Hip fracture analgesia and fascia iliaca block in ED
result.setting: Emergency department, Macclesfield District General Hospital
result.standard: NICE CG124 and RCEM guidance: FICB performed where applicable (100%); contraindications documented if FICB not performed (100%); pain re-evaluation within 30 minutes of analgesia (100%)

cycle1.result: FICB performed 26/40 (65%); contraindications documented in 0/14 (0%) without FICB; pain re-evaluation within 30 min 21 (52.5%); mean time to first analgesia 130 ± 28.8 min; mean time to FICB 228 ± 36.2 min.

result.intervention: Practical sessions to familiarise ED clinicians with FICB, and a mandatory analgesia checklist for all suspected neck of femur fractures (pain scores, analgesia times, FICB details and reason if not given).

cycle2.result: FICB performed 26/40 (65%, p=0.74); contraindications documented in 9/14 (64.3%); pain re-evaluation within 30 min 20 (50%, p=0.99); mean time to first analgesia 38.8 ± 13.2 min (p<0.001); mean time to FICB 63.4 ± 19.1 min (p=0.002).

result.other_findings: FICB uptake and pain re-evaluation did not improve despite faster analgesia. No FICB-related complications in either cycle.

result.setting: Non-specialist admitting district hospital (Warrington and Halton Teaching Hospital, per affiliation); emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics, referring to a tertiary spinal centre
result.standard: Local standard operating procedure for acute back pain with suspected cauda equina syndrome, based on BASS/SBNS guidance (senior ED discussion, anal tone and perianal sensation documented, MRI within 24 hours, spinal centre plan documented); no target stated

cycle1.result: ED assessment and senior discussion 24 (96%); discussion with spinal centre by senior ED doctor 13 (61.9%); anal tone documented 23 (92%); perianal sensation documented 18 (72%); spinal centre plan documented per SOP 5 (20%); MRI within 24 hours 25 (100%).

result.intervention: Teaching on CES and neurological examination for T&O and ED juniors, posters of the pathway in ED, discussion between T&O and ED on GP referrals, and emails to staff; an electronic SBAR documentation template was also created.

cycle2.result: ED assessment and senior discussion 26 (90%, p=0.727); discussion by senior ED doctor 2 (9%, p=0.000); anal tone documented 28 (97%, p=0.887); perianal sensation documented 28 (97%, p=0.028); spinal centre plan documented 0 (0%, p=0.033); MRI within 24 hours 29 (100%).

result.other_findings: Referral by a senior ED doctor and documentation of the spinal centre plan worsened, which the authors linked to COVID-19 staffing pressures. Discussion with the spinal centre, post-MRI discussion and management per advice stayed at 100%.

result.topic: Weight-bearing after periprosthetic femoral fracture surgery
result.setting: Dorset County Hospital, district general hospital trauma and orthopaedics; data from the Hip Fracture Registry
result.standard: British Hip Society guidance: aim for full weight-bearing in the immediate postoperative period; no target stated

cycle1.result: 28 (73.7%) had surgery (19 ORIF, 9 revision). Of these, 22 (78.6%) were full weight-bearing, 4 (14.3%) limited weight-bearing and 2 (7.2%) non-weight-bearing. One fixation failure (3.5%).

result.intervention: Results presented at a local orthopaedic educational meeting on aiming for immediate full weight-bearing; no re-audit reported.
result.other_findings: Limited and non-weight-bearing instructions often lacked specific functional restrictions and duration, making rehabilitation difficult. The single fixation failure occurred in a patient allowed full weight-bearing.

result.topic: DVT diagnostic pathway (D-dimer and Wells score)
result.setting: Royal London Hospital, nurse-led Fast Response Team outpatient clinic for suspected lower limb DVT
result.standard: Modified Wells rule (low Wells score with negative D-dimer to avoid ultrasound); re-audit against the local revised diagnostic algorithm; no target stated

cycle1.result: 510 (96.9%) had D-dimer and ultrasound results; 265 (51.9%) negative D-dimer, of whom 143 (53.9%) had a low Wells score. 7 of 143 with negative D-dimer and low Wells score had a DVT, all with a risk factor not in the Wells score; none without risk factors had a DVT (NPV 100%).

result.intervention: Revised clinical diagnostic algorithm adding assessment of extra risk factors to the Wells score; ultrasound omitted in patients with negative D-dimer, low Wells score and no risk factors.

cycle2.result: All 290 (100%) had complete results; 94 (32.4%) negative D-dimer, 43 with low Wells score, of whom 30 had risk factors and were scanned. 1/94 (1%) with negative D-dimer had a DVT (on OCP). 13 of 290 (4.5%) not scanned under the algorithm; all negative D-dimer patients had probability score and risk factors recorded.

result.other_findings: The D-dimer assay changed between cycles, lowering the proportion of negative results. The re-audit saved £767.

result.setting: Queen's Hospital, Burton upon Trent; emergency department and fracture clinic
result.standard: NICE guidance for children's distal radius buckle fractures: removable splint instead of full cast and no routine follow-up; no target stated

cycle1.result: ED: 0% splint (all back slab). Fracture clinic: 62 (95.4%) full cast, 3 (4.6%) splint. Discharged at first visit 5 (7.7%); second visit 56 (86.2%); third visit 4 (6.2%).

result.intervention: New ED and fracture clinic pathway (splint or soft cast with information leaflet and no follow-up), posters in ED and fracture clinic, and email reminders to staff.

cycle2.result: ED: 17 (19.5%) splint, 70 (80.4%) back slab. Fracture clinic: 44 (50.6%) converted to splint and 2 remained in splint (53%), 41 (47.1%) cast. Discharged at first visit 39 (44.8%); second visit 48 (55.2%).

result.other_findings: Discharge at first visit remained suboptimal. Some casts were used because of limited splint sizes, patient preference or lack of technicians at weekends.

result.setting: Department of Orthopaedics, University Hospital Tuebingen
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean HVA 36.4 degrees preoperatively, 3.5 at 2 days and 13.4 at 6 weeks (p<0.001); mean IMA 16.8, 6.4 and 9.8 degrees (p<0.001). Possible non-union in 4 patients (2.6%) at 6 weeks.

result.other_findings: Residents operated in 65 minutes versus 45 minutes for attending surgeons, with no significant radiographic differences. No hardware failure or wound complications.

result.topic: Post-operative weight-bearing after hip fracture surgery
result.setting: National Hip Fracture Database aggregate data from 169 hospitals in England, Wales and Northern Ireland
result.standard: NICE hip fracture guideline (2011): early unrestricted weight-bearing after surgery; no target stated

cycle1.result: 93.2% full weight-bearing, 3.1% (2310) non-weight-bearing and 3.6% not recorded. Nine hospitals made 10% or more of cases non-weight-bearing; one site recorded 100% non-weight-bearing.

result.other_findings: Reasons for non-weight-bearing are not recorded by the NHFD. The highlights give the full weight-bearing figure as 93.8%.

result.topic: Marker ball placement on pelvic radiographs
result.setting: Poole General Hospital trauma unit (district general hospital); AP pelvic radiographs for intracapsular neck of femur fractures
result.standard: Local trauma unit guideline: marker ball entirely visible and placed between the femurs inferior to the symphysis pubis; agreed target 80% for each

cycle1.result: Marker ball present in 27 (45%). Of these, entirely visible 16 (59%) and correctly positioned 11 (41%); overall compliance 59% (n=16).

result.intervention: Poster reminders in radiography areas, a presentation to the radiography team by a T&O registrar, and a mandatory checklist for all such X-rays.

cycle2.result: Marker ball present in 39 (78%). Entirely visible 33 (84%, p=0.042) and correctly positioned 32 (82%, p=0.0014); overall compliance 80% (n=31, p=0.132), meeting the target.

result.other_findings: The methods state the first cycle was completed in June 2025, overlapping the re-audit dates given in the abstract. No inter-observer reliability testing was done.

result.setting: Galway University Hospitals, tertiary referral centre; consent forms for emergency orthopaedic trauma surgery
result.standard: American Association of Orthopaedic Surgeons 'Orthopaedic Surgical Consent' standards (name, DOB, board number, procedure without abbreviation, side/site stated); no target stated

cycle1.result: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 79 (74.5%). Side/site 81 (76.4%) (the abstract wording says 'without correctly stating' but the comparison treats this as compliance). Abbreviation and side/site both failing in 13 (12.3%).

result.intervention: A single 90-minute virtual education session for all trauma and orthopaedic staff on consent standards, sharing cycle 1 results.

cycle2.result: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 37 (92.5%, p=0.02). Side/site correctly stated 39 (97.5%, p=0.0015). No form had both failures (0% vs 12.3%, p=0.02).

result.other_findings: Only 106 of 147 and 40 of 57 consent forms were available for review. The abstract gives the cycle 1 sample as 107.

result.setting: Vancouver General Hospital, acute hospital; patients coded as subtrochanteric femoral fractures
result.standard: Published diagnostic criteria for atypical femoral fracture; no target stated

cycle1.result: Of 204 patients coded as subtrochanteric fractures, 178 had radiographic evidence of other fracture types. Of 193 with radiographs reviewed, 24 (12.4%) met AFF criteria; radiologists had diagnosed AFF in only 1 of the 24.

result.other_findings: 75% of AFF patients were on bisphosphonates. 12 of 19 (63%) with contralateral femur imaging had a contralateral focus of periosteal/endosteal new bone.

result.setting: Orthopaedics, Kent and Sussex Hospital, Tunbridge Wells; foundation-year doctors starting orthopaedic posts
result.standard: Orthopaedic consultants' expectations of basic knowledge, assessed by a test; no target stated

cycle1.result: Knowledge was inadequate against consultants' basic expectations (no figures in abstract).

result.intervention: A focused 2-week teaching programme at the start of the orthopaedic job.

cycle2.result: Standards improved significantly on a different retest (no figures in abstract).

result.other_findings: Junior doctors' confidence and enjoyment of the specialty also increased. Only the abstract was available.

result.topic: ENT casualty management of common acute presentations
result.setting: ENT casualty service of a tertiary referral hospital (Mater Dei Hospital, Msida)
result.standard: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries (otitis externa), ENT UK nasal trauma guidance, ENT UK position statement and AAO-HNS guideline (SSNHL), British Rhinological Society epistaxis guideline; e.g. audiogram within 24 hours for SSNHL, nasal fracture review within 7 days

cycle1.dates: 5 weeks (10 consecutive weeks over both cycles)
cycle1.result: Tympanic membrane integrity documented in otitis externa 34.3%; nasal fracture reviewed within 7 days 58.3%, MUA within 14 days 92.9%; SSNHL audiogram within 24 hours 33.3%; epistaxis cautery for visible vessel 87.2%, documentation of counselling 28.0%.

result.intervention: Web-based ENT toolkit with QR-code access in casualty, condition-specific pathways, structured documentation templates, procedure checklists and diagrams, introduced to FY doctors at induction with a short training session.

cycle2.result: Tympanic membrane documentation 67.7% (p = 0.002); nasal fracture review within 7 days 94.7% (p = 0.006), MUA within 14 days 100% (p = 0.31); SSNHL audiogram within 24 hours 80.0% (p = 0.09); epistaxis cautery 98.1% (p = 0.03), counselling documented 46.0%.

result.other_findings: Unnecessary imaging and swabbing fell (e.g. avoidance of unnecessary nasal imaging 41.7% to 84.2%); counselling documentation in epistaxis stayed low at 46.0%. Staff confidence rose from 2.4/5 to 4.1/5; cycles involved different FY cohorts.

result.setting: National postal survey of UK spinal surgeons (members of BASS or Society for Back Pain Research)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Survey of practice: 79% had a routine post-operative regime, 35% gave written instructions, 55% did not refer for physiotherapy after discharge; restrictions on lifting, sitting and driving varied widely.

result.other_findings: 89 surgeons surveyed, 57% usable response; weak correlation between individual surgeons' activity restriction recommendations.

result.topic: Lying and standing blood pressure in falls assessment
result.setting: Orthopaedic rehabilitation ward, district general hospital in North East England
result.standard: NICE falls guidance: completion of falls assessment and lying and standing blood pressure measurement; target 100%

cycle1.result: Falls assessment completed 38/41 (93%); lying and standing BP recorded 14/41 (34%).

result.intervention: Cycle 1 results presented at departmental teaching, daily reminders at the morning huddle, educational flyers and targeted education for doctors, nurses and healthcare staff.

cycle2.result: Falls assessment completed 40/41 (98%) (p = 0.61); lying and standing BP recorded 28/41 (68%) (p = 0.004).

result.other_findings: Systolic drop of 20 mmHg or more found in 5/14 (36%) then 13/28 (46.4%) of those measured. LSBP was sometimes marked as completed in the falls assessment when it was not done.

result.specialty: Orthopaedics – Oncology (giant cell tumour of bone)
result.topic: Neoadjuvant denosumab biosimilar in giant cell tumour of bone
result.setting: Tertiary cancer centre (Mahamana Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya Cancer Centre and Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital, Varanasi)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Retrospective case series: two doses of denosumab biosimilar gave a mean lesion size reduction of 17.75% ± 8.029%; sclerotic rim in all 17 cases; local recurrence 2/17 (11%) and distant recurrence 2/17 (11%).

result.other_findings: No hypocalcaemia or osteonecrosis; both recurrences were in previously recurrent cases treated by repeat extended curettage.

result.topic: Fluoroscopy radiation exposure in distal radius fracture fixation
result.setting: William Harvey Hospital, Ashford, Kent (East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean screening time 24 seconds (range 0.1-111), mean 43 exposures (range 5-209), mean DAP 4.75 µGy·m² (range 0.31-29.26), mean air kerma 0.26 (range 0.01-9).

result.other_findings: No significant differences by surgeon grade (registrar vs consultant) or fracture type; 39 of 145 cases excluded because no fluoroscopy data were saved. No standard or diagnostic reference level was available to audit against.

result.specialty: Oral and maxillofacial surgery / trauma epidemiology
result.topic: Head and neck trauma admissions epidemiology
result.setting: Muhimbili National Hospital, Dar es Salaam (national referral hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Most common diagnoses: S02 fracture of skull and facial bones 277 (44.1%), S05 injury of eye and orbit 114 (18.2%), S09 other head injuries 77 (12.3%); 81.2% male.

result.other_findings: Head and neck trauma was 2.55% of all trauma admissions; no seasonal trend.

result.setting: Poole Hospital, district general hospital (University Hospitals Dorset)
result.standard: Clark's Positioning in Radiography criteria for lateral wrist radiographs (styloid superimposition, anatomical inclusion, piso-scapho-capitate relationship); target 80% for each

cycle1.result: Styloid superimposition 72% (36/50); anatomical inclusion 98% (49/50); piso-scapho-capitate relationship 50% (25/50).

result.intervention: Poster on positioning technique in the radiology department and trauma meeting rooms, and a formal teaching session by an associate specialist hand surgeon for radiographers and orthopaedic doctors.

cycle2.result: Styloid superimposition 92% (46/50) (p = 0.047); anatomical inclusion 100% (50/50) (p = 0.992); piso-scapho-capitate relationship 82% (41/50) (p = 0.014).

result.other_findings: All three standards met the 80% target at re-audit; the study did not assess whether any injuries were missed.

result.setting: Emergency department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham (tertiary centre)
result.standard: BESS guideline and local hospital policy: orthogonal post-reduction views (AP plus axillary or scapular Y view)

cycle1.result: Adequate orthogonal post-reduction radiographs in 5/22 (22.7%, 95% CI 10.1-43.4); 17/22 (77.3%) inadequate, with inadequacy recognised by resident doctors in 2/17 (11.8%).

result.other_findings: No imaging request explicitly specified two orthogonal views and no repeat imaging was obtained in the ED; education and re-audit are planned.

result.setting: Elective arthroplasty unit, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Hyponatraemia protocol based on NICE guidance (sodium cut-off 133 mmol/l per local guidance); no numeric target stated

cycle1.result: Hyponatraemia in 36 (12%); only 38% of hyponatraemic patients investigated, 33% had endocrine input; mean 3.6 days to endocrine referral; length of stay 7.7 vs 4.6 days; 4 of 11 profound cases admitted to critical care (8 days in total).

result.intervention: Direct endocrine pathway developed with endocrinology based on NICE guidance: protocol poster displayed in clinical areas and agreement for same-day endocrine review of arthroplasty patients referred via ICE.

cycle2.result: Hyponatraemia in 31 (11.7%); all 3 profound cases investigated and referred to endocrinology; mean 2.3 days to endocrine referral; length of stay reduced by 0.7 days (p = 0.008144); no critical care admissions (p = 0.031622).

result.other_findings: Hyponatraemia was more common after knee than hip replacement and in older patients in both cycles; symptoms and fluids were not assessed in cycle 2.

result.setting: Mansell Road Practice, primary care general practice, London
result.standard: NICE guidance on bone protection (bisphosphonates first line) after fragility fracture

cycle1.result: 33/47 on bone protection agents (26 bisphosphonate plus calcium/vitamin D, 7 bisphosphonate alone); 2 on calcium/vitamin D alone; 12/47 on neither therapy.

result.intervention: Educational poster on recognition and coding of fragility fractures; untreated patients reviewed individually and started on treatment, referred for DEXA or specialist advice.
result.other_findings: Of the 12 untreated, 2 were miscoded; of the remaining 10, 4 were referred for DEXA, 2 referred for zoledronic acid and 1 started alendronic acid. No re-audit reported.

result.setting: Consultant orthopaedic surgeons in training hospitals across the Republic of Ireland (online survey)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Survey of practice (response 69/96, 72%): 72.5% aware of local VTE guidelines, 37.8% aware of national guidelines; 90% routinely used mechanical prophylaxis; 74% used LMWH for inpatients; 82.6% discharged patients on extended chemical prophylaxis.

result.other_findings: No national trauma VTE guideline existed in Ireland at the time; 67% agreed that defensive medicine drives VTE prophylaxis emphasis; agents and durations were highly heterogeneous.

result.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley
result.standard: BOA guidance on ward round documentation (patient ID and name, ward round clinician, documenting clinician, grade, date, time, whom to contact)

cycle1.result: Paper notes: patient ID and name 29 (65.91%); documenting clinician 17 (38.64%); time of ward round 26 (59.09%); grade of ward round clinician 18 (40.91%); whom to contact 0 (0%) (percentages as stated).

result.intervention: Introduction of electronic ward round record keeping.

cycle2.result: Electronic records: patient ID and name, ward round clinician, documenting clinician, date, time and grade all 34 (100%); whom to contact 5 (14.70%).

result.other_findings: Staff satisfaction and educational value scores (44 staff surveyed) were higher for electronic records; documentation of whom to contact stayed poor.

result.setting: Trauma theatre, Trauma and Orthopaedic Department of a district general hospital (Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley)
result.standard: BOAST guidance on the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets (2021): document skin condition and isolation method, pressure SBP + 50-100 mmHg upper limb and + 70-130 mmHg lower limb in adults, ischaemic time under 120 minutes

cycle1.result: Skin status documented 37%; isolation method documented 43%; tourniquet pressure documented 71%; pressure within BOAST safe limit 25%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; tourniquet details made a mandatory part of the electronic operation note template; labels on tourniquet machines to calculate pressure; BOAST guidance posted in the theatre doctors' office.

cycle2.result: Skin status documented 69% (p = 0.004); isolation method 74% (p = 0.003); pressure documented 94% (p = 0.003); pressure within BOAST safe limit 75%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.

result.other_findings: Mean pressure above SBP fell from 125.9 to 99.9 mmHg (upper limb) and 154.2 to 121.7 mmHg (lower limb); about 25% still used pressures above the recommended range and surgeons not using the template still omitted details.

result.topic: Lying and standing blood pressure in falls assessment
result.setting: Orthopaedics department (ethical approval from Salisbury District Hospital)
result.standard: NICE guidelines on falls in older people: lying and standing blood pressure measurement; RCP FFAP guidance on LSBP procedure

cycle1.result: LSBP measured in 16 (32%); correctly documented in 12/16 (75%).

result.intervention: Results presented at geriatric medicine mortality meeting with root cause analysis; flyers and posters on wards, teaching sessions for ward staff on LSBP measurement and recording on POET, and aide-memoires placed around wards.

cycle2.result: LSBP measured in 45 (83.3%) (p < 0.0001); correctly documented in 45 (100%) (p = 0.0035).

result.other_findings: Root cause analysis found insufficient staff training and need for assistance to stand patients post-operatively.

result.setting: Elective orthopaedic ward, University College London Hospitals
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists guidance and PRSB eDischarge Summary Standard: investigation (imaging) results included in discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Imaging results documented in 0/144 (0%) discharge summaries.

result.intervention: Audit feedback poster on national standards for resident doctors, and a mandatory 'diagnostic imaging' field added to the electronic discharge summary template.

cycle2.result: Imaging results documented in 118/127 (92.9%) discharge summaries.

result.other_findings: Accuracy and clinical usefulness of the documented imaging were not assessed; trauma admissions were excluded.

result.topic: Neurovascular assessment documentation in limb fractures
result.setting: Russell Hall Hospital (Trauma and Orthopaedic admissions)
result.standard: BOAST Peripheral Nerve Injury guideline (December 2021): documentation of specific nerve and arterial status; target 100%

cycle1.result: Any NV documentation 43/49 (87.8%); detailed neurological findings 19/49 (38.8%); detailed vascular findings 13/49 (26.5%).

result.intervention: Single educational awareness presentation on the consequences of poor NV assessment (May 2024).

cycle2.result: Any NV documentation 47/48 (97.9%) (p = 0.053); detailed neurological findings 26/48 (54.2%) (p = 0.129); detailed vascular findings 22/48 (45.8%) (p = 0.048).

result.other_findings: Many entries still used the nonspecific phrase 'NV intact' rather than nerve-specific and arterial details.

result.topic: Empiric antimicrobial prescribing in trauma ICU
result.setting: Level I Trauma Intensive Care Unit, Inkosi Albert Luthuli Central Hospital, Durban
result.standard: Local surveillance-based empiric antimicrobial policy with antimicrobial stewardship

cycle1.result: Of 101 empiric and 14 directed prescriptions, excluding multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter, 87 (93.5%) were appropriate and 6 (6.5%) incorrect; ultrabroad-spectrum combination therapy used in 11 patients but necessary in only 2.

result.other_findings: 106/227 (46.6%) patients had culture-positive isolates; ESBL in 19% of E. coli and 25% of Klebsiella; 18 MRSA isolates. Abstract only.

result.setting: Pinderfields General Hospital, Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust (large district general hospital)
result.standard: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission (National Hip Fracture Database)

cycle1.result: Surgery within 36 hours 54%; mean time to surgery 43.68 hours; BPT achieved in 45.7%; trust ranked 152/160 for time to surgery.

result.intervention: Anaesthetic 'hot week' introduced in January 2018: the same anaesthetist covers hip fracture lists, attends trauma meeting, liaises with orthopaedic and orthogeriatric teams and advises on medical optimisation.

cycle2.result: Surgery within 36 hours 87.5%; mean time to surgery 25.11 hours; BPT achieved in 84%; ranking rose to 20th for time to surgery and 18th for BPT.

result.other_findings: Rescheduled operations fell from 126 to 31 and mean length of stay fell by 5.1 days; mortality unchanged. The unit sees on average 551 hip fractures a year. Abstract only.

result.setting: Department of Neurosurgery, Aga Khan University (single institution), elective spinal arthrodesis
result.standard: Cross-matched to transfused (C/T) ratio compared with the optimal 2:1 reported in the literature

cycle1.result: 292 units of packed red cells cross-matched, 66 transfused (C/T ratio 4.4:1); 39 of 85 patients (45.88%) transfused. C/T 6.9:1 for degenerative disease and 23:1 for cervical spine.

result.intervention: Recommended a blood ordering schedule: two units for preoperative haemoglobin <9 g/dl, trauma, adult idiopathic scoliosis or more than two levels; group and hold for the rest. Not re-audited.
result.other_findings: On multivariate analysis only indication for surgery was independently associated with transfusion (AIS adjusted OR 124.87, trauma 34.37 versus degenerative disease).

result.setting: Trauma unit, district general hospital (University Hospitals Dorset, Poole)
result.standard: BOAST and radiographic positioning criteria for a true lateral ankle view (four criteria); target 100% for each

cycle1.result: Criterion 1 (fibula superimposed by posterior tibia) 83%; criterion 2 (talar domes superimposed) 61%; criterion 3 (open uniform tibiotalar joint) 69%; criterion 4 (landmarks included) 99%.

result.intervention: Posters in the emergency department and orthopaedic on-call room/radiography suites, and a teaching session by a foot and ankle associate specialist for orthopaedic staff and radiographers.
result.other_findings: Talar dome superimposition remained the hardest criterion to meet; the usual failure of criterion 4 was omission of the base of the fifth metatarsal.

result.topic: Preoperative medication administration when nil by mouth
result.setting: Trauma theatre list patients on orthopaedic/surgical wards, Basildon University Hospital
result.standard: Local and national (Royal College of Anaesthetists) guidance that preoperative trauma patients receive prescribed medications while nil by mouth, except anticoagulants, ACE inhibitors and ARBs

cycle1.result: 16/41 (39%) received their medications correctly; 22 critical drug class omissions; 19 omitted because nil by mouth.

result.intervention: Poster on drug trolleys listing which medications to give or withhold, meetings with ward managers and nursing staff, and presentation at orthopaedic and anaesthetic audit meetings.

cycle2.result: 25/41 (61%) received their medications correctly; 10 critical drug class omissions; 12 omitted because nil by mouth.

result.other_findings: Being nil by mouth was the main reason for omission; the abstract states 40 patients in the first round while the text gives 41.

result.setting: Orthopaedic department, James Paget University Hospital (district general hospital), elective and trauma lists
result.standard: Local standard from patient survey: a patient should be seen by the same surgeon from preoperative clinic to surgery and postoperative follow-up

cycle1.result: Same surgeon throughout 23%; same team 43%; operated on by clinic surgeon 50%; followed up by operating surgeon 40%; trauma continuity 10%.

result.intervention: Trauma on-call rota reorganised to weekly consultant 'on take' so the admitting team operates, and ward clerk booked follow-up into the operating surgeon's clinic.

cycle2.result: Same surgeon throughout 24%; same team 56%; operated on by clinic surgeon 60%; followed up by operating surgeon 43%; trauma same team 75%.

result.other_findings: A survey of 1000 outpatients found 92% wanted the same surgeon in clinic and theatre and 94% wanted follow-up by the operating surgeon. Individual surgeon continuity barely changed.

result.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff (teaching hospital), on-call handover
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England 'Safe Handover' minimum dataset and BMA guidance; gold standard 100% data transmission and 100% proforma compliance

cycle1.result: Handwritten plain paper sheets: patient labels used 73% (35/48); side of injury handed over in 28/49; tasks performed or outstanding 31% (15); relevant blood results 19% (6/32); overall data handed over 72.6%.

result.intervention: Standardised handover proforma based on the RCS dataset, piloted (version 1, 78% compliance), revised after junior doctor feedback and implemented as version 2.

cycle2.result: 100% proforma compliance; labels 96% (53/55); side of injury 98% (54/55); tasks 100% (55/55); relevant blood results 20% (6/29); overall data handed over 93.2% (p<0.01).

result.other_findings: Handover of relevant blood results stayed poor, possibly because the form had no dedicated field for it. The abstract reports label use as 72.9% to 93.4%.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, King's Mill Hospital, Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; inpatients aged 65+ with hip fracture
result.standard: NICE: cognitive assessment (AMTS or 4AT) within 24 hours of admission for hip fracture patients aged 65 and over, with regular postoperative assessment

cycle1.result: Admission AMTS within 24 hours 15 (78.9%); postoperative AMTS 18 (94.7%); postoperative 4AT 9 (47.4%); no postoperative delirium.

result.intervention: Educational posters with QR codes for AMTS and 4AT calculators on wards and doctors' office, and a staff training session for doctors.

cycle2.result: Admission AMTS 29 (96.7%); postoperative AMTS 26 (86.7%); postoperative 4AT 18 (60.0%); postoperative delirium 6 (20.0%).

result.other_findings: Postoperative 4AT documentation remained well below full compliance.

result.setting: Orthopaedic wards, University Hospital Lewisham (London teaching hospital), adult inpatients
result.standard: Trust treatment escalation plan (TEP) policy: TEP completed for emergency adult admissions, within 48 hours

cycle1.result: Overall TEP completion 69.5%; completed within 48 hours 47.82%; mean time to complete 4.4 days; mean overrides 3.2; longest 35 days; 24 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 30.4% (n=7).

result.intervention: Revised local TEP pathway/algorithm allowing F1+ doctors to complete TEPs for young patients with simple fractures, algorithm displayed in trauma room, emails, individual teaching, and reminders to discuss TEP status on the post-take ward round.

cycle2.result: Overall completion 88.2%; completed within 48 hours 35.29%; mean time 3.7 days; mean overrides 1.3; longest 13 days; 5 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 11.76% (n=2).

result.other_findings: Completion within 48 hours fell between cycles despite better overall completion. A junior doctor questionnaire found TEPs were skipped because of competing clinical priorities.

result.topic: Ottawa knee rules compliance in radiograph requests
result.setting: Emergency department and orthopaedic referrers, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (high-volume trauma centre)
result.standard: Ottawa Knee Rules (endorsed by NICE and RCR iRefer) documented in knee radiograph requests; target 100%

cycle1.result: At least one OKR criterion documented 41%; age >=55 52%; fibular head tenderness 3%; isolated patellar tenderness 13%; inability to flex to 90 degrees 3%; inability to bear weight 14%. Adequate documentation: orthopaedic SHOs/registrars 35.7%, ENPs/ANPs/triage 52.4%.

result.intervention: Posters and leaflets in clinical areas, presentations at departmental meetings, formal and informal teaching, and emails summarising the rules.

cycle2.result: At least one OKR criterion 91% (p<0.01); age 62%; fibular head tenderness 68%; patellar tenderness 72%; inability to flex 65%; inability to bear weight 57%. Adequate documentation: orthopaedic SHOs/registrars 92.9%, ENPs/ANPs/triage 88.2%.

result.other_findings: 9% of cycle 2 referrals still lacked adequate documentation; authors suggest OKR prompts in the electronic request system.

result.setting: Regional trauma and tertiary referral centre, Galway University Hospitals; acute orthopaedic trauma admissions
result.standard: Irish HSE Standards and Recommended Practices for Healthcare Records Management and HSE National Model of Care for Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery documentation standards (checklist)

cycle1.result: Unscripted notes: consultant on call 78% (39/50); time of injury 72% (36/50); associated injury 48% (24/50); smoking status 86% (43/50); alcohol 42% (21/50); vital signs 28% (14/50); other systems 14% (7/50).

result.intervention: Standardised admission proforma developed with multidisciplinary stakeholders after results were presented at departmental teaching, with an accompanying education session; one-month introduction period.

cycle2.result: Proforma notes: consultant on call 100% (p=0.0005); time of injury 100% (p=0.0001); associated injury 100% (p=0.0001); smoking 100% (p=0.0001); alcohol 94% (p=0.0001); vital signs 70% (p=0.0001); other systems 74% (p=0.0001).

result.other_findings: Admitting doctor grade documentation fell from 92% to 82% and vital signs remained incomplete at 70%. A poll of 16 Irish units found admission proforma use in only 18.8%.

result.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic unit, St Helens and Knowsley Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (teaching hospital); records of the clinical audit department
result.standard: NICE principles for best practice in clinical audit: every audit should complete the cycle with re-audit (100%)

cycle1.result: Of 61 audits, 12 (19.7%) abandoned, 44 (72.1%) presented and 5 (8.2%) ongoing; audit cycle completed by re-audit in only 13 (29%).

result.intervention: Recommendations only (signed undertaking by audit lead, reallocation to a new trainee, email reminders of re-audit dates, consultant supervision); no re-audit reported.
result.other_findings: A consultant led or supervised 59% of audits; 7 of 12 abandoned audits had no reason recorded. Hip fracture was the commonest topic (19.7%).

result.topic: Baseline DEXA scanning in breast cancer
result.setting: Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley (district general hospital); newly diagnosed breast cancer
result.standard: NICE guideline 80: baseline DEXA for early invasive breast cancer starting aromatase inhibitors, with treatment-induced menopause or starting ovarian ablation/suppression; target 100%

cycle1.result: 100 patients sampled, 66 with early/locally invasive cancer, 42 with an indication; 16/42 (38%) had a DEXA scan. Of those scanned 8/16 (50%) osteopaenic and 1/16 (6%) osteoporotic.

result.intervention: Results presented to surgical and oncology departments and the breast MDT, posters summarising the guideline in breast clinics and MDT areas, and MDT discussion of the need for DEXA.

cycle2.result: 11/11 (100%) indicated patients received a DEXA scan (17 early breast cancers).

result.other_findings: Earlier re-audits: January 2014 9/10 (90%) and February 2014 12/13 (92%). 16% of records were incomplete and excluded.

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis after non-arthroplasty knee surgery
result.setting: Joint replacement unit, tertiary orthopaedic hospital (University Hospitals Dorset / Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital affiliations); elective non-arthroplasty knee procedures
result.standard: NICE VTE guidance: prophylaxis after arthroscopy if anaesthetic time 90 minutes or more (or VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk), and after all other non-arthroplasty knee surgery; target 100%

cycle1.result: Arthroscopy with anaesthetic time >90 minutes 2/4 (50%) received prophylaxis; other non-arthroplasty surgery 9/25 (36%).

result.intervention: Formal teaching session for the joint replacement unit team by a senior consultant on recording anaesthetic time, weight-bearing status and VTE prescription on operation notes and postoperative instructions.
result.other_findings: No VTE events were reported. The text states both 56 and 66 patients for the second loop; authors suggest a VTE checklist with discharge summaries.

result.topic: Tranexamic acid use in knee arthroplasty
result.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Good Hope Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham (elective surgical hub)
result.standard: NICE: combined topical and intravenous tranexamic acid in knee arthroplasty for patients without renal impairment (1 g IV only with significant renal impairment)

cycle1.result: TXA used in 20 (48.8%), not used in 21 (51.2%); combined IV and topical 3 (7.3%); IV only 14 (34.1%); topical only 3 (7.3%).

result.intervention: Targeted emails to consultants and registrars, presentation at a specialty meeting, and posters on TXA and NICE guidance on computers across the elective surgical suite.

cycle2.result: TXA used in 38 (73.1%) (p=0.016), not used in 14 (26.9%); combined IV and topical 16 (30.8%) (p=0.005); IV only 22 (42.3%).

result.other_findings: In cycle 2 non-use was 20% (8/40) without a tourniquet versus 50% (6/12) with one. In significant renal impairment TXA was omitted in 8/9 (cycle 1) and 6/12 (cycle 2).

result.setting: Trauma orthopaedic unit, Salford Care Organisation (Northern Care Alliance NHS hospital); adult trauma surgery
result.standard: Northern Care Alliance 2023 orthopaedic antibiotic prophylaxis guideline (choice, timing within 60 minutes, duration) and NICE NG180 (blood pressure within 20% of baseline, core temperature 36.5-37.5°C); 100% target for timing and blood pressure

cycle1.result: Correct intraoperative antibiotic 68/104 (65.4%); given within 60 minutes 104/104 (100%); postoperative duration compliant 67/104 (64.4%); overuse 25/104 (24%); blood pressure within target 104/104 (100%); temperature documented 36/104 (35%).

result.intervention: Planned: EPR alerts for antibiotic choice and duration, mandatory temperature documentation fields, staff education and a compliance dashboard; re-audit planned in six months.
result.other_findings: Postoperative compliance was lowest in joint replacement (40%, overuse 37%) and best in internal fixation (75%); all documented temperatures were normothermic.

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis after hip and knee arthroplasty
result.setting: Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley (district general hospital); elective total hip and knee replacement discharge summaries
result.standard: NICE VTE guidance: THR 28 days LMWH plus anti-embolism stockings until discharge; TKR 14 days LMWH plus stockings

cycle1.result: THR 23/25 (92%) and TKR 20/23 (87%) received enoxaparin plus stockings; overall compliance 90%.

result.intervention: Arthroplasty discharge pack displayed as posters and handouts at the arthroplasty station, regular teaching sessions on NICE discharge guidance, and final check of discharge letters by the nurse in charge.

cycle2.result: THR 24/24 (100%) and TKR 22/23 (96%) correct; overall compliance 98%.

result.other_findings: Overall compliance was calculated as the average of the THR and TKR rates; patient outcomes were not recorded.

result.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Sunderland Royal Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 29 patients had preoperative echo versus 40 random non-echo controls (from 349 hip fractures). Mean delay to surgery 2.7 days (range 0-6) with echo versus 1.1 days (range 0-3) without (p<0.001); no difference in length of stay (16.7 vs 15.4 days, p=0.14) or 30-day mortality (p=0.41).

result.intervention: Departmental guidelines for expediting echo requests in hip fracture patients with a murmur and a liaison with cardiology to prioritise them; no re-audit reported.
result.other_findings: No patient needed preoperative cardiac intervention; 14 had an aortic valve abnormality including 2 severe and 1 critical aortic stenosis, and 10% had no valvular pathology.

result.setting: Urgent treatment centre and emergency departments of two district general hospitals
result.standard: AO Foundation guidance: ankle immobilised in neutral plantigrade position; acceptable tibia-to-sole angle 80-100 degrees on lateral radiograph

cycle1.result: Mean angle 108.5 degrees (SD 11.7); 18/65 (27.7%) within 80-100 degrees (DGH 1 n=32, DGH 2 n=33).

result.intervention: Single interactive session led by plaster technicians (for UTC nurses at DGH 1 and for ED junior doctors at DGH 2) plus educational posters where plastering occurred.

cycle2.result: Mean angle 106.2 degrees (SD 11.9) (p=0.285); 23/61 (37.7%) within 80-100 degrees (p=0.231) (DGH 1 n=28, DGH 2 n=33).

result.other_findings: Acceptable casts improved by 22% at the site that trained UTC nurses but only 3% at the site that trained junior doctors; angles were measured by a single reviewer.

result.setting: Tibetan Delek Hospital, Dharamsala (small general hospital without on-site obstetricians); all labour admissions
result.standard: Hospital policy of active management of the third stage of labour; WHO partogram use for labour management and transfer decisions

cycle1.result: Postpartum haemorrhage 7 (12%); retained placenta 3 (5%); 11 (19%) transferred, 8 (75%) for 'failure to progress' in uncomplicated primiparous women; no partograms used.

result.intervention: Staff retraining in active management of the third stage with intramuscular Syntometrine at delivery of the anterior shoulder, introduction of the WHO partogram with training, and feedback seminars, one-to-one sessions and newsletter reports after each cycle.

cycle2.result: PPH 5 (6%); retained placenta 0; 6 (7%) transferred, 1 (17%) for failure to progress; partograms used in 77 (86%), complete and accurate in 13 (17%).

result.other_findings: Interim audits: 1997 (n=110) PPH 6%, partogram use 80% with 30% unhelpful; 1998 (n=65) PPH 5%, partogram use 87% with 60% complete. Partogram quality declined by 2003 after staff turnover.

result.topic: Vertebral fragility fracture reporting on CT
result.setting: UK-wide Royal College of Radiologists national audit with the Royal Osteoporosis Society and Royal College of Physicians; radiology departments
result.standard: RCR national audit of reporting vertebral fragility fractures (Genant grading) on non-trauma CT including the thoracolumbar spine in patients over 70

cycle1.result: Moderate/severe vertebral fragility fractures reported in 26%.

result.intervention: A series of UK-wide interventions between audits (details not given in the abstract).

cycle2.result: Moderate/severe vertebral fragility fractures reported in 32%; VFF incidence 21.7%; improvements across all patient-related and organisational parameters.

result.other_findings: Each site reviewed 50-100 consecutive CT studies. Modelling predicts 23,420 extra diagnoses, 562 hip fractures prevented in year one with treatment and a potential saving of £13,207,000.

result.topic: Bone protection after fragility fracture in the very elderly
result.setting: North Staffordshire Fracture Liaison Service; patients aged 85 and over with fragility fracture, GP prescribing
result.standard: FLS policy in line with national guidance: GP letter advising empirical oral bisphosphonate for patients aged 85 and over after fragility fracture

cycle1.dates: Fractures December 2018 to October 2020; data collected October 2020
cycle1.result: 160/396 (40%) prescribed a bisphosphonate (median 9 months after fracture); over 90% alendronic acid.

result.intervention: Standard GP letter rewritten using GP feedback to address barriers, including advice on relative contraindications and referral.

cycle2.dates: Fractures December 2020 to May 2021; data collected July 2021
cycle2.result: 38/74 (51%) prescribed a bisphosphonate (median 5 months after fracture).

result.other_findings: 408 eligible patients in cycle 1, with Summary Care Record data for 396. Different fracture-to-audit intervals between cycles limit comparison.

result.topic: Tranexamic acid in hip fracture surgery
result.setting: Dorset County Hospital, Dorchester; district general hospital
result.standard: NICE guideline: offer TXA to adults having surgery expected to cause moderate blood loss (>500 ml)

cycle1.result: 26/37 (70.0%) eligible patients received intraoperative TXA; contraindication documented in 0%

result.intervention: Local hip fracture protocol updated to include TXA, targeted teaching for anaesthetic and theatre staff, and encouragement to record contraindications

cycle2.result: 23/27 (85.2%) received TXA; contraindication documented in 7.4%; difference not significant (Fisher's exact p = 0.23, OR 0.41)

result.other_findings: No thromboembolic complications in either cycle; transfusion and outcome data were not collected.

result.topic: Postoperative analgesia protocol compliance in arthroplasty
result.setting: Whittington Hospital, London; elective hip and knee arthroplasty in an enhanced recovery programme
result.standard: Local enhanced recovery multimodal postoperative analgesia protocol for elective hip and knee replacement

cycle1.dates: One week at the beginning of July 2014
cycle1.result: 0/27 patients received all medications according to the protocol

result.intervention: Electronic prescribing order set (JAC) for the analgesia protocol introduced in August 2014; results presented, re-education of rotating junior staff and protocol added to induction documentation

cycle2.result: Total compliance 58%; gabapentin 96%, modified-release morphine 96%, weak opioid 100%, conversion to PRN analgesia 100%, ibuprofen 58%

result.other_findings: Intermediate cycle in October 2014 (n=26) showed compliance of 34.6% (p<0.001); ibuprofen prescribing stayed poor, with 9/26 omitted without documented contraindication.

result.setting: Hull University Teaching Hospitals; emergency department and fracture clinic
result.standard: NICE guideline: manage paediatric distal radius buckle fractures with a soft cast and discharge directly from the ED

cycle1.result: 33/84 discharged at first visit; 69 had a single X-ray, 12 had two and 4 had three X-rays

result.intervention: Results presented to the department and ED; parents educated on fracture type and cast removal with option to forgo clinic visits; safety brochures; email reminders to fracture clinic staff about NICE guidance

cycle2.result: 62/64 discharged directly from the ED (42 focal rigidity cast removed at home, 10 backslab, 10 crepe bandage); 2 returned to plaster room and 1 to fracture clinic

result.other_findings: Extra visits, radiographs and cast changes in the first audit cost £18,078 over 6 months.

result.topic: Intrathecal fentanyl and postoperative opioid use after hip arthroplasty
result.setting: Complexo Hospitalario Universitario de A Coruña; primary total hip arthroplasty under spinal anaesthesia
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean PACU morphine use 4.76 mg (0 µg fentanyl, n=25), 4.39 mg (10 µg, n=255) and 7.33 mg (>10 µg, n=12), P=0.029; about 25% in each group needed opioids on the ward within 48 h

result.other_findings: Described as a clinical audit but is a retrospective association analysis without a standard.

result.topic: Virtual MDT decision time in acute arthroplasty
result.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust; tertiary referral centre for complex arthroplasty
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean time to decision via Siilo secure messaging 0.87 days versus conventional weekly MDT wait of 3.9 days; mean saving 3.03 days per case

result.other_findings: Commonest diagnoses were periprosthetic fracture (28), knee PJI (16) and dislocation (12); MDT wait was an estimated, not measured, comparator.

result.setting: Croydon University Hospital; planned orthopaedic trauma lists
result.standard: All intraoperative images available on PACS within 72 hours of being taken (local target)

cycle1.result: 9/27 (33%) images available within 72 hours; 4 (15%) delayed by failure to request, 14 (52%) requested but not processed

result.intervention: Radiographers told not to screen without a valid request; tick box added to trauma list submission template; agreement with radiology to upload within 72 hours; radiographers invited to trauma meeting; changes communicated by email and governance meetings

cycle2.dates: Two weeks, six weeks after the first post-intervention cycle
cycle2.result: 90% of images processed within 72 hours; delays from failure to request eliminated

result.other_findings: First post-intervention cycle (n=15) showed images not available fell from 66.0% to 13.3%.

result.setting: University Hospital Waterford; regional orthopaedic trauma service
result.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England record-keeping standards (GSP 2014); target 80% or more for all aspects

cycle1.result: Poor documentation of 50% of aspects: author name 50%, date 70%, medications 20%, functional status 30%, investigation results 30%, social history 40%, systemic review 75%

result.intervention: Orthopaedic admission proforma introduced and discussed at morbidity and mortality meeting; then dedicated slots in departments and printable from any hospital computer

cycle2.result: Author name 100%, date 100%, medications 95%, social history 70%, functional status 65%, systemic review 90%, investigation results 35%

result.other_findings: Three cycles over 6 months (60 notes); investigation results stayed poor as results often not available at admission.

result.topic: COVID-19 impact on hip fracture services
result.setting: 185 units in 14 countries (national audits in Germany, Scotland and Ireland plus online survey)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 102/160 (63.7%) units reported worse service quality; 74/160 (46.2%) had >50% reduction in theatre access; 135/160 (84.4%) reported reduced theatre efficiency

result.other_findings: Two thirds lost specialist orthopaedic nurses, a third lost orthogeriatric services and a quarter lost physiotherapists.

result.setting: Two district general hospitals without spinal units (London and KSS deaneries)
result.standard: Local standards of 95% for neurological examination, management plan, stability, permitted mobility and precautions documentation

cycle1.result: No criterion met the standard; hospital 1: neurological examination 74%, stability 44%, precautions 53%, permitted mobility 26%, delay in treatment 59%, serious medical concern 37% (7/19)

result.intervention: Spinal injuries proforma and ASIA chart placed on trust computers, introduced via M&M presentations, email and face-to-face; desktop icon added

cycle2.result: Hospital 1: neurological examination 100%, stability 95%, precautions 100%, permitted mobility 95%, delay in treatment 11%, serious medical concern 6% (1/18)

result.other_findings: Proforma used in 96% (hospital 1) and 100% (hospital 2) in first eight weeks; re-audit at hospital 2 ongoing.

result.topic: Hip fracture best practice tariff compliance
result.setting: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; acute hip fracture service
result.standard: National Hip Fracture Database best practice tariff criteria (surgery within 36 h, orthogeriatric review within 72 h, pre- and post-operative AMT, etc.)

cycle1.result: BPT achieved in 8/18 (44.4%); 4 waited >36 h for surgery, 7 >72 h for orthogeriatric review, 9 lacked both AMT scores; FI block in ED 3/18 (16.7%)

result.intervention: Eight-page multidisciplinary clerking booklet, hip fracture care group, twice-weekly consultant orthogeriatric ward rounds, and booklet in local induction

cycle2.result: BPT achieved in 22/24 (91.7%); all had both AMT scores; FI block in ED in 6

result.other_findings: Booklet used in 27/30 (90%) but ED section complete in only 20 (74.1%); mean acute stay fell from 18.9 to 16.4 days (p=0.066).

result.setting: Galway University Hospital; fracture clinic
result.standard: NICE NG38: buckle fractures treated with non-rigid cast or splint without routine follow-up

cycle1.result: 59 fracture clinic visits; mean 1.9 visits per child

result.intervention: Parents taught about fracture type and soft cast removal and offered no further visits; information leaflet designed with plaster technicians and nurses
result.other_findings: Authors recommend implementing the guidance in A&E as well as fracture clinics.

result.topic: Vertebral fragility fracture reporting on CT
result.setting: 127 UK radiology departments (RCR national audit); 50 consecutive non-trauma CT studies each
result.standard: RCR audit standards: comment on vertebrae 100%, fracture severity, recommended terminology 'vertebral fracture' 100%, appropriate referral 100%

cycle1.result: 79% of reports commented on vertebrae; severity mentioned in 26.2%; recommended terminology in 60.1%; onward referral recommended in 2.6%

result.other_findings: 1362/6357 (21.4%) had a fracture on auditor review.

result.setting: Central Norfolk Older Adult Inpatient Unit, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines (2012): fracture risk assessment with FRAX or QFracture for women aged 65 and over

cycle1.result: 0% had documented FRAX/QFracture assessment or DEXA; only 19% on bone-protecting medication despite over 90% intermediate or high risk

result.other_findings: Described as a re-audit but earlier results are not reported; 60% had secondary risk factors and about 70% a history of falls.

result.topic: Surgical site infection prevention in hand and wrist trauma
result.setting: 45 hospitals in 12 countries via the Reconstructive Surgery Trials Network
result.standard: WHO global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infection

cycle1.result: Surgical hand preparation 91%, drapes and gowns 92%, standard postoperative dressings 98%; adherence low for other antimicrobial practices

result.other_findings: Adherence varied significantly across criteria.

result.topic: AI detection of proximal femoral fractures
result.setting: Royal Adelaide Hospital; external validation at Stanford University Medical Center
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Model AUC 0.994 versus 0.969 for five radiologists; external validation AUC 0.980

result.other_findings: Algorithmic audit found an operating-point shift on external validation and more errors in abnormal bones such as Paget's disease.

result.topic: Clinician fracture detection on whole-body radiographs
result.setting: Two Level 1-equivalent public-sector trauma units, Cape Town
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Fracture detection rate 89% (95% CI 86–93%); 21 fractures missed, including all elbow fractures (3/3) and 9/13 shoulder girdle fractures

result.other_findings: One missed fracture clearly needed surgery and 7 others might have.

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis in foot and ankle surgery
result.setting: 68 UK centres (UK-FATE national prospective audit)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 3630 (31.95%) received no chemical anticoagulation; LMWH 6303 (84.4% of those treated), factor Xa inhibitor 10%, aspirin 4.1%; VTE 1.1% (83/7469) in those anticoagulated

result.other_findings: No significant difference in VTE between anticoagulant types; 6 weeks was the commonest duration (64.50%).

result.setting: Center of Orthopaedics and Traumatology, University Hospital Brandenburg/Havel; tertiary setting
result.standard: JBI evidence-based audit criteria for selection and administration of intra-articular knee injections

cycle1.result: Low adherence with all audit criteria, including informed patient decision-making and recommending alternative treatments

result.intervention: Educational briefings for physicians and informative flyers for patients

cycle2.result: Substantial improvements in several criteria, including stepwise referral to conservative therapy and injection content

result.other_findings: Numbers not given in the abstract.

result.topic: Malnutrition in overweight hip fracture patients
result.setting: Dedicated hip fracture unit, The Prince Charles Hospital, Brisbane
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Malnutrition prevalence 18.3%; 12-month mortality 17.3%; malnutrition increased odds of 12-month mortality (OR 4.47, p=0.020)

result.other_findings: Malnutrition also linked to delirium (OR 3.64) and delayed mobilisation (OR 3.29).

result.setting: Female later life psychiatry ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and National Osteoporosis Guideline Group guidance on identification, assessment and management of fragility fracture risk

cycle1.result: FRAX calculated in 8/16 (50%) without known osteoporosis; FRAX communicated to GP in 2/8 (25%)

result.intervention: Fracture risk scoring added to structured ward round template and osteoporosis information posters displayed

cycle2.result: FRAX calculated in 15/17 (88%); FRAX communicated to GP in 11/15 (73%); BMD measured in 1/10 (10%) intermediate-risk patients

result.other_findings: None of the 4 high-risk patients were started on bisphosphonates.

result.setting: Broadmoor Hospital, high secure forensic psychiatry hospital, 15 wards
result.standard: Local trust guideline: vitamin D checked within one month of admission and then three-monthly, with dosing by level

cycle1.result: 76.4% checked within one month of admission; 66.7% checked in last 3 months; 21.4% correct dose, 22.9% under-dosed, 14.3% over-dosed, 41.4% no dose when indicated

result.other_findings: Deficiency fell from 43.6% at admission to 14.5% on most recent levels.

result.setting: Orthopaedic operating theatre, Regional Headquarter Hospital Skardu
result.standard: WHO surgical hand hygiene guidelines

cycle1.result: Scrub duration at least two minutes 45%, coverage of all surfaces 50%, proper antiseptic use 60%, correct drying 55%, overall aseptic protocol 70% (about 40 staff)

result.intervention: Live demonstrations of correct hand scrubbing and visual reminder posters in the scrub area

cycle2.result: Scrub duration 90%, coverage 88%, antiseptic use 93%, drying 87%, overall aseptic protocol 95%; all improvements statistically significant

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: 140 Australian facilities contributing Surgical National Antimicrobial Prescribing Survey audits
result.standard: Surgical NAPS appropriateness assessment of surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis

cycle1.result: Overall appropriateness 58.0% of 6709 doses; procedural 64.7%, postprocedural 48.3%

result.other_findings: Commonest reasons for inappropriateness were timing of procedural doses (50.9%) and duration of postprocedural prescriptions (49.8%).

result.setting: Jai Prakash Narayan Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS, New Delhi; tertiary trauma centre
result.standard: College of American Pathologists guidelines for FFP transfusion

cycle1.result: Appropriate FFP use 49.5%

result.other_findings: Orthopaedics accounted for 12.6% of FFP use; neurosurgery had the highest appropriate use (50.5%).

result.setting: 61 NHS hospital trusts; colorectal, orthopaedic, urological and gynaecological surgery
result.standard: Enhanced Recovery protocol elements; good compliance defined as 80% or more

cycle1.result: Compliance weakly associated with shorter stay (r -0.18 colorectal, -0.14 orthopaedics, -0.25 gynaecology); 80% compliance linked to 2, 1 and 3 day shorter median stay in colorectal, orthopaedic and urological surgery

result.other_findings: No length of stay saving in gynaecology.

result.setting: Single centre; Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: British Orthopaedic Association-endorsed consent guidance (12 potential risks)

cycle1.result: 4/12 risks documented in <50% of intracapsular fractures (n=35) and 7/12 in <50% of extracapsular fractures (n=35)

result.intervention: Raising awareness and attaching consent guidance; neck of femur fracture-specific consent form then implemented

cycle2.result: 100% documentation of potential risks in intracapsular and extracapsular fractures

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Multicentre quality improvement registry (16 institutions, 26 surgeons)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Stiffness in 4.2%; surgery for stiffness in 1.1%; loss of extension 3.8%, loss of flexion 3.1%

result.other_findings: Stiffness linked to longer tourniquet time (93.0 vs 78.8 min) and anteriorly displaced meniscal tears.

result.setting: 3 major trauma centres and 5 trauma units
result.standard: BOA and BAPRAS standards for trauma (open fractures)

cycle1.result: Antibiotics within 1 hour 41.7%; splint in ED 74.4%; documented orthoplastic plan 85.8%; debridement within 12 hours for high-energy injuries 41.7%
